text: Chose JSON Schema tool definitions with strict mode over free-form function calls after 4% of agent outputs produced unparsable arguments under load.
label: decision

text: Tool calls are defined as Anthropic tools with strict JSON Schema input definitions validated by pydantic on the server before dispatch to the handler registry.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Promptfoo for offline regression runs because ad-hoc Jupyter evaluations made diffs between prompt versions impossible to review.
label: decision

text: Prompt changes trigger a Promptfoo CI job that runs 400 fixture prompts against the new and old prompt variants and publishes a diff report to the PR.
label: architecture

text: Chose Gitleaks in a pre-receive hook over a nightly scan after a leaked API token made it into main and took six hours to notice.
label: decision

text: The Git server enforces a Gitleaks pre-receive hook with a custom rule set and quarantine pushed refs until the scan exits cleanly.
label: architecture

text: Adopted OpenFeature with a flagd provider over LaunchDarkly for non-customer-facing flags because the team wanted on-cluster evaluation and no egress.
label: decision

text: Feature flags are served by flagd sidecars per pod reading a Git-synced ConfigMap, with SDKs talking localhost:8013 via the OpenFeature SDK.
label: architecture

text: Chose self-hosted Sentry over the SaaS offering after data-residency requirements from the EU customer demanded no telemetry leaving Frankfurt.
label: decision

text: Exceptions are captured by a self-hosted Sentry 24 deployment on eu-central-1 with ClickHouse for events and an 11-day retention per project.
label: architecture

text: Picked Vector over Fluent Bit for log shipping after the memory footprint under 30k events/s made Fluent Bit OOM on the smaller nodes.
label: decision

text: Logs flow from each node via a Vector DaemonSet through a Kafka transform topic and into Loki, with a parallel sink to S3 for long-term archival.
label: architecture

text: Moved from standalone Prometheus to Mimir after cardinality from per-user labels pushed the single instance past 50 GB of head series.
label: decision

text: Metrics are written by Prometheus agents remote-writing to a Grafana Mimir cluster with four ingesters, three store-gateways, and S3 long-term blocks storage.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Okta for workforce SSO because the previous Google Workspace-only setup could not integrate with the new SOC 2 session policies.
label: decision

text: All internal tools authenticate via Okta SAML with a 12-hour session, device-trust verification, and SCIM provisioning into the employee directory.
label: architecture

text: Chose NS1 managed DNS over Route 53 because latency-based steering across multiple cloud providers required per-answer filter chains.
label: decision

text: External DNS is hosted on NS1 with filter-chain records performing geo, latency, and up/down health checks across AWS, GCP, and on-prem origins.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Fastly in front of S3 because the product team needed edge compute with VCL to handle signed-URL rewrites closer to the user.
label: decision

text: Static assets and media segments are served via Fastly with a custom VCL service that validates short-lived HMAC tokens before hitting origin S3 buckets.
label: architecture

text: Switched the monorepo from Lerna to Turborepo 2 after build times on a twelve-package workspace exceeded twenty minutes on developer laptops.
label: decision

text: The TypeScript monorepo is orchestrated by Turborepo 2 with a remote cache hosted on Vercel, task graph derived from package.json, and pnpm workspaces underneath.
label: architecture

text: Chose Vitest over Jest for the darkraise-ui package after ESM support and Vite HMR made the prior Jest setup impossible to maintain.
label: decision

text: Frontend unit tests run under Vitest 1.6 with happy-dom, parallelized across eight workers and reporting coverage via v8 into a JUnit XML for CI.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Ruff over Flake8 and isort because running three tools on every commit doubled pre-commit latency and caused developers to skip hooks.
label: decision

text: Python linting runs a single Ruff 0.5 invocation configured in pyproject.toml with E, F, I, UP, and B rule sets and an auto-fix stage in the pre-commit hook.
label: architecture

text: Switched from pip-tools to uv after lockfile resolution on the backend service dropped from 90 seconds to under three.
label: decision

text: Python environments are managed with uv 0.4, using a pyproject.toml plus uv.lock checked into git and an in-CI uv sync --frozen to install deterministic dependencies.
label: architecture

text: Chose Harbor over Docker Hub Enterprise for internal images because CVE scanning and project-level RBAC were both required for the FedRAMP audit.
label: decision

text: Internal container images live in a Harbor 2.10 registry with Trivy scanning, Notary signing, and replication to a warm standby registry in a second region.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Consul over Kubernetes Services because bare-metal VMs outside the cluster still had to participate in the same service catalog.
label: decision

text: Service discovery is centralized in a Consul cluster of five servers with Consul agents on every VM and Kubernetes pod, exposing DNS on the local node at 127.0.0.1:8600.
label: architecture

text: Picked Terraform Enterprise over Pulumi because the platform team had ten years of HCL modules that could not realistically be rewritten.
label: decision

text: Infrastructure is codified in Terraform 1.8 modules stored in a central repository, executed by Terraform Enterprise workspaces with Sentinel policies and Vault-issued cloud credentials.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Changesets for versioning because manual npm publish commits kept going out of sync across the five public packages in the repo.
label: decision

text: The monorepo publishes packages via Changesets with a GitHub Action that opens a Version Packages PR, then runs changeset publish to npm on merge to main.
label: architecture

text: Chose Alembic with a single-head policy over bespoke SQL files after a merge produced two concurrent head revisions that broke production on deploy.
label: decision

text: Database migrations are versioned with Alembic, enforced single-head by a CI check, and applied during a dedicated pre-deploy Kubernetes Job before rollout.
label: architecture

text: Adopted SLSA level 3 provenance on all release binaries after a supply-chain tabletop exercise revealed no way to verify which commit produced a given image.
label: decision

text: Release pipelines emit SLSA v1.0 provenance attestations signed by Sigstore cosign and stored alongside images in the OCI registry under the .att tag.
label: architecture

text: Chose Cloudflare Workers over AWS Lambda for the URL-shortener edge tier because cold starts dominated p95 latency at 400 ms on Lambda.
label: decision

text: The URL-shortener runs as a Cloudflare Worker deployed to the global network with Workers KV for hot lookups and a D1 database as the durable store.
label: architecture

text: Adopted TimescaleDB over vanilla Postgres for IoT telemetry after ingest past 40k rows/second caused lock contention on the btree indexes.
label: decision

text: IoT telemetry is written to a TimescaleDB 2.15 hypertable chunked by one-hour intervals with continuous aggregates refreshed every five minutes for dashboard queries.
label: architecture

text: Picked Avro with a Confluent Schema Registry over raw JSON on Kafka after two consumer teams silently diverged on the order-created payload.
label: decision

text: Kafka topics carry Avro-encoded messages validated against a Confluent Schema Registry with BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE compatibility and subject naming of <topic>-value.
label: architecture

text: Moved to trunk-based development after two long feature branches collided during a release freeze.
label: decision

text: All engineers commit to main behind feature flags; short-lived branches merge within 24 hours and the release is cut from main every Thursday.
label: architecture

text: We chose mandatory two-reviewer approval after a silent auth regression slipped through a single-approver merge last quarter.
label: decision

text: Pull requests require two human approvals plus a green CI run before the merge queue will accept them; the CODEOWNERS file routes security-sensitive paths to the platform team.
label: architecture

text: We adopted a merge queue because concurrent PR merges kept breaking main two or three times per week.
label: decision

text: GitHub's merge queue serialises integration: each PR is rebased onto the tip, re-runs the full test matrix, and only lands if the pipeline stays green for the whole sequence.
label: architecture

text: We moved from biweekly trains to daily releases once the smoke-test pipeline dropped below ten minutes.
label: decision

text: Every green build on main promotes to staging at 10:00 UTC and to production at 15:00 UTC on business days, gated by an automated canary analysis that watches error rate and latency for fifteen minutes.
label: architecture

text: We adopted a commander-plus-scribe-plus-comms role split after our first SEV1 lasted four hours because nobody was driving.
label: decision

text: Every SEV1 page opens a dedicated Slack channel, assigns an incident commander, a scribe, and a communications lead; the commander owns technical decisions while the scribe keeps a running timeline for the postmortem.
label: architecture

text: We chose a follow-the-sun rotation because the EU on-call was paging at 3 AM twice a week.
label: decision

text: Three regional rotations cover US-West, EU, and APAC in eight-hour windows; the primary on-call owns acknowledgement within five minutes and handoffs happen in a shared channel with an explicit written summary of open incidents.
label: architecture

text: We dropped two-week sprints in favour of continuous flow after retros kept surfacing the same end-of-sprint crunch.
label: decision

text: Work is tracked on a single pull-based board with explicit work-in-progress limits per column; weekly demos replace sprint reviews and planning happens as a thirty-minute backlog refinement each Monday.
label: architecture

text: We adopted CODEOWNERS-enforced ownership after an orphaned service caused a seven-hour outage with no clear responder.
label: decision

text: Every top-level directory maps to exactly one owning team in CODEOWNERS; ownership changes require a signed ADR and the platform team audits the mapping quarterly against the service catalog.
label: architecture

text: We introduced a lightweight RFC process after three teams independently built their own feature-flag systems in the same quarter.
label: decision

text: Any change with cross-team impact lands as a markdown RFC in the architecture repo, collects comments for five business days, and is ratified by the principal engineers' group before implementation begins.
label: architecture

text: We switched to blameless postmortems after engineers started hiding near-misses to avoid being named in the writeups.
label: decision

text: Every SEV2-and-above incident gets a written postmortem within five business days; the document focuses on contributing factors and systemic fixes, names no individuals as at fault, and its action items are tracked to completion in the issue tracker.
label: architecture

text: We moved to structured interviews with calibrated rubrics after a hiring manager audit showed wildly different bars across loops.
label: decision

text: Every candidate goes through the same four stages: recruiter screen, a coding exercise, a system-design round, and a values interview; each stage has a written rubric and two interviewers must independently submit scores before the debrief.
label: architecture

text: We chose a buddy-plus-checklist onboarding model after new hires reported feeling lost for their entire first month.
label: decision

text: Each new engineer is paired with a buddy for thirty days, works through a written onboarding checklist covering environment setup, first PR, first on-call shadow, and first incident readout, and checks in weekly with their manager against that list.
label: architecture

text: We set a four-hour review SLA after throughput data showed PRs sitting unreviewed for a median of two business days.
label: decision

text: Pull requests awaiting review ping the owning team's channel after four business hours and escalate to the team lead after eight; a weekly dashboard tracks the median time-in-review per team.
label: architecture

text: We adopted a Friday and holiday-eve deploy freeze after three Friday deploys turned into weekend incidents.
label: decision

text: Production deploys are blocked from Friday 14:00 UTC through Monday 09:00 UTC and for twenty-four hours before recognised holidays; exceptions require the on-call director's written approval in the deploy channel.
label: architecture

text: We made rollback the default response for production SEV1s after a forward-fix attempt doubled the length of the outage.
label: decision

text: Any SEV1 that correlates with a recent deploy triggers an automatic rollback within ten minutes unless the incident commander explicitly opts for a forward-fix and documents the reason in the channel.
label: architecture

text: We introduced a flag-expiry policy after discovering more than two hundred stale flags that nobody remembered owning.
label: decision

text: Every new feature flag is created with an owner and an expiry date; a weekly job opens a tracking ticket for any flag past its expiry and flags more than ninety days old fail the release readiness check.
label: architecture

text: We adopted an error-budget-based freeze rule after the reliability team and product kept arguing about when to slow feature work.
label: decision

text: Each service has a monthly error budget derived from its SLO; once the budget is exhausted feature deploys are automatically blocked and only reliability fixes ship until the rolling window recovers.
label: architecture

text: We made threat modelling a required gate after a high-severity data-exposure bug shipped without any security sign-off.
label: decision

text: Features touching authentication, authorization, or PII require a written threat model reviewed by the security team before implementation begins; the review is linked from the RFC and tracked on the release checklist.
label: architecture

text: We started requiring pairing on critical-path changes after a solo refactor of the payments module caused a two-hour incident.
label: decision

text: Any change to code paths tagged critical in the service catalog is authored in a pairing session; the pairing partner co-signs the PR and the session is noted in the commit trailer.
label: architecture

text: We moved retros from ad-hoc to biweekly after three months of retros happening only when something went wrong.
label: decision

text: Each squad runs a sixty-minute retrospective every second Friday using a start-stop-continue template; action items are captured in the team board and the squad lead reviews progress against them at the next retro.
label: architecture

text: We shifted from annual to semi-annual performance reviews after engineers said yearly feedback came too late to act on.
label: decision

text: Performance reviews run every six months on a fixed calendar; each review combines manager assessment, peer feedback from three nominated colleagues, and a self-reflection, all captured in the HR system for continuity.
label: architecture

text: We adopted an inner-source model after platform teams became a bottleneck for every cross-team feature request.
label: decision

text: Shared infrastructure repositories accept pull requests from any engineer in the company; each repo has a published contributing guide, a maintainer rotation, and an SLA for first response on outside contributions.
label: architecture

text: We made design review mandatory for all services with customer-facing APIs after two teams shipped incompatible webhook shapes.
label: decision

text: Any service exposing an external API runs a design review with the API council before the first endpoint ships; the council checks naming, versioning, error shape, and rate-limit defaults against the company API guidelines.
label: architecture

text: We moved to expand-contract migrations after a destructive alter-table locked the orders database for twenty minutes.
label: decision

text: Schema changes ship in two deploys: the first adds the new shape and dual-writes, the second removes the old shape after a verified backfill; destructive statements run only behind a feature flag and a documented rollback script.
label: architecture

text: We adopted a monthly dependency upgrade train after a six-month-stale library left us exposed to a published CVE.
label: decision

text: A scheduled job opens upgrade PRs the first Monday of each month for every direct dependency; the platform team triages and merges them by the end of that week, and any unmerged upgrades roll into the next month's review.
label: architecture

text: We made docs a release-blocker after an incident revealed the runbook for a tier-one service hadn't been updated in a year.
label: decision

text: Each service has a runbook and an architecture page owned by the same team that owns the code; a CI check fails the deploy if either page has not been touched in the last ninety days and the service had a code change in that window.
label: architecture

text: We formalised escalation levels after an on-call engineer struggled alone on a customer-visible outage for ninety minutes.
label: decision

text: Every SEV1 escalates to the secondary on-call after ten minutes without acknowledgement, to the engineering manager after thirty, and to the director after sixty; the escalation path is encoded in the pager policy and tested monthly via game days.
label: architecture

text: We adopted a weekly bug bash plus a rotating triage role after the backlog crossed one thousand open issues.
label: decision

text: A triage engineer rotates weekly across the squad and owns all incoming bugs: every new issue is labelled, severity-scored, and either routed to a milestone or closed within two business days, and the team spends Friday afternoons on a themed bug bash.
label: architecture

text: We introduced a weekly experiment council after three A/B tests shipped with overlapping audiences and unreadable results.
label: decision

text: Every experiment is registered in the experiment platform before launch and reviewed in a Tuesday council meeting; the council checks audience overlap, power analysis, and stopping criteria, and signs off before the flag is turned on.
label: architecture

text: We chose Black plus Ruff on autoformat after a style debate dominated three consecutive engineering all-hands.
label: decision

text: Every Python repository runs Black and Ruff in a pre-commit hook and in CI; style discussions in PRs are closed by pointing at the configured tooling and any rule change requires a one-line RFC in the style repo.
label: architecture

text: We set a coverage floor on changed lines only after a blanket eighty-percent rule pushed teams to write useless tests.
label: decision

text: The CI check enforces that at least seventy-five percent of lines changed in a PR are exercised by tests; whole-file coverage is reported as a trend but does not block merges, keeping the incentive on testing new work.
label: architecture

text: We separated security incidents from reliability incidents after a credential leak got lost in the general ops channel.
label: decision

text: Security incidents follow a distinct runbook and page the security team first; the response channel is access-controlled, evidence is preserved in a dedicated bucket, and legal is looped in within the first hour for any data-exposure class.
label: architecture

text: We made accessibility review a launch gate for customer-facing UI after an external audit found WCAG violations on the checkout flow.
label: decision

text: Every customer-visible UI change is reviewed against the WCAG 2.2 AA checklist by the accessibility guild before launch; automated axe-core tests run in CI and block merges on new violations.
label: architecture

text: We chose to buy rather than build for observability tooling after the internal metrics stack consumed half of an SRE team for a year.
label: decision

text: Observability runs on a vendor platform with a clear integration layer; the SRE team owns the integration and dashboards while product engineers consume the tooling through a thin internal SDK, freeing the team to focus on reliability work.
label: architecture

text: We moved to ephemeral preview environments after a shared staging cluster became the bottleneck for every large feature.
label: decision

text: Each PR spins up its own namespaced environment on the dev cluster with seeded data; the environment is torn down automatically when the PR merges or after forty-eight hours of inactivity, and a shared long-lived staging is reserved for end-to-end regression tests.
label: architecture

text: We adopted a written kickoff doc for every epic after multiple features shipped without clear success criteria.
label: decision

text: Each epic begins with a one-page kickoff doc covering problem statement, success metrics, non-goals, and rollout plan; engineering manager, product manager, and tech lead all sign off before the first ticket is opened.
label: architecture

text: We reserved twenty percent of each quarter for tech-debt work after two years of debt tickets never making it into sprints.
label: decision

text: Each team's quarterly plan allocates a dedicated debt bucket equal to one in five engineer-weeks; debt items are prioritised by the tech lead and reported alongside feature progress in the quarterly business review.
label: architecture

text: We locked down production shell access after an accidental rm on a live host caused a two-hour data recovery effort.
label: decision

text: Direct shell access to production hosts is disabled; engineers use an audited break-glass tool that opens a time-boxed session, records every command, and requires a peer's approval before granting elevated privileges.
label: architecture

text: We introduced a formal vendor review after a shadow-IT SaaS purchase exposed customer data to an unvetted processor.
label: decision

text: Any new third-party service that touches customer or production data goes through a joint security, legal, and procurement review; approved vendors are listed in a shared registry and renewals trigger an automatic re-review.
label: architecture

text: We adopted quarterly OKRs after yearly goal-setting kept drifting out of relevance by the third month.
label: decision

text: Each team sets three to five objectives with measurable key results at the start of every quarter; progress is reviewed at a mid-quarter checkpoint and scored publicly at the end, and the results feed into the next quarter's planning.
label: architecture

text: We replaced change advisory board approval with automated release readiness checks after CAB meetings added a day of latency with no measurable safety gain.
label: decision

text: Releases are approved by an automated readiness pipeline that verifies green tests, a signed-off runbook entry, an up-to-date rollback script, and the absence of active incidents; exceptions still require a director's written approval.
label: architecture

text: We committed to writing ADRs for every significant choice after an architecture quiz showed half the team could not explain why we picked Kafka.
label: decision

text: Architecture decisions land as numbered ADRs in the docs repo using the context-decision-consequences template; every PR that introduces a new service or replaces an existing one must link to the relevant ADR, and the index is reviewed at the quarterly architecture summit.
label: architecture

text: We introduced a weekly Friday demo after stakeholders complained they only saw finished work at quarter boundaries.
label: decision

text: Every Friday at 16:00 local, each squad shows a fifteen-minute demo of shipped or shippable work; recordings go to a shared Drive folder and the engineering newsletter links the week's highlights for asynchronous viewers.
label: architecture

text: We adopted a monthly game day after a region-failover drill revealed nobody had actually tested the DNS switch under load.
label: decision

text: Each month one squad runs a pre-announced game day that injects a realistic failure mode in staging and, quarterly, in production under a tight blast radius; findings are tracked as normal incidents with owned remediation items.
label: architecture

text: We introduced a runbook drill after an on-call engineer couldn't follow an outdated Redis failover doc during a real page.
label: decision

text: Each tier-one service's runbook is exercised by its on-call once per quarter in a staging drill; any step that doesn't work is fixed inside the drill window and the runbook's last-verified date is stamped at the top of the page.
label: architecture

text: We committed to upstreaming internal patches after maintaining a private fork of a key library consumed weeks of engineer time every upgrade.
label: decision

text: Every internal patch to an external dependency is opened as a pull request upstream within two weeks; until it lands we track the fork in a shared board and the platform team owns keeping the fork rebased against the upstream main branch.
label: architecture

text: We started a biweekly engineering talk after survey feedback flagged lack of cross-team technical visibility.
label: decision

text: A thirty-minute engineering talk runs every other Wednesday with a rotating speaker drawn from the signup sheet; talks are recorded, slides are archived in the learning repo, and attendance is optional but counted towards the growth rubric.
label: architecture

text: We adopted a shared experiment log after three teams re-ran the same onboarding experiment unaware of each other's results.
label: decision

text: Every experiment writes an entry in the company-wide experiment log with hypothesis, setup, result, and decision; the log is searchable by feature area and new experiment proposals must check for prior art before approval.
label: architecture

text: We moved promotions to a calibrated committee review after manager-only promotions produced noticeable inconsistencies between teams.
label: decision

text: Promotion packets are written against a public rubric by the candidate's manager, reviewed by a cross-team committee that calibrates against anonymised past packets, and decided in a single meeting that produces a written rationale for each outcome.
label: architecture

text: We dropped formal change approval forms in favour of a lightweight change log after the forms became copy-paste rituals everyone ignored.
label: decision

text: Every production-impacting change posts a structured message in the change channel with author, scope, rollback plan, and monitoring link; the log is archived for audit and reviewed in the weekly reliability meeting for patterns.
label: architecture

text: Moved from self-managed Kubernetes to GKE Autopilot after the fourth CVE scramble in a quarter cost us two weekends.
label: decision

text: Workloads run on a GKE Autopilot cluster in europe-west1 fronted by a global HTTPS load balancer with Cloud Armor WAF rules.
label: architecture

text: Chose AKS over EKS for the new Azure commitment; the existing Enterprise Agreement absorbed the control plane cost entirely.
label: decision

text: The staging cluster is an AKS deployment in westeurope with three node pools: system, general workloads, and GPU-tainted inference nodes.
label: architecture

text: Swapped Calico for Cilium after the eBPF datapath benchmarks showed 30 percent lower p99 latency on east-west traffic.
label: decision

text: Pod networking runs on Cilium in kube-proxy-replacement mode with Hubble exporting flow logs to the observability cluster.
label: architecture

text: Decided to keep Route 53 for public zones and CoreDNS for cluster-internal resolution instead of unifying on one provider.
label: decision

text: Public records live in Route 53 with health-checked failover while in-cluster lookups resolve via CoreDNS with a stub zone for corp.internal.
label: architecture

text: Moved gRPC ingress off ALBs onto NLBs after HTTP/2 connection reuse repeatedly pinned pods on a single target for minutes.
label: decision

text: gRPC traffic terminates on an NLB in each region which forwards to Envoy ingress pods that handle TLS and per-method routing.
label: architecture

text: Chose Cloudflare over Fastly for the CDN layer because bundled bot management and WAF were a single contract.
label: decision

text: Static assets and image origin are fronted by Cloudflare CDN with cache-key normalisation and a same-origin worker injecting CSP headers.
label: architecture

text: Dropped the Docker shim on worker nodes in favour of containerd after Kubernetes 1.24 made the deprecation final.
label: decision

text: All nodes run containerd 1.7 with the systemd cgroup driver; image pulling goes through a Harbor mirror on the same subnet.
label: architecture

text: Migrated the colo hypervisors from VMware vSphere to Proxmox VE once the Broadcom licensing hike made renewal untenable.
label: decision

text: The colo runs two Proxmox VE clusters of four nodes each with Ceph RBD as the shared storage backend for live migration.
label: architecture

text: Replaced the CloudFormation stacks with Terraform so we could manage AWS, GCP, and Cloudflare from one tool and one state backend.
label: decision

text: Infrastructure is defined in Terraform with state stored in an S3 bucket plus DynamoDB locks, organised into per-environment workspaces.
label: architecture

text: Picked Pulumi with TypeScript over another Terraform rollout because the platform team wanted real types and unit tests on stack outputs.
label: decision

text: The platform code is a Pulumi TypeScript monorepo that exposes a handful of component resources wrapping AWS, GitHub, and Datadog providers.
label: architecture

text: Retired the self-hosted HashiCorp Vault cluster in favour of AWS Secrets Manager; the ops cost of two Vault outages per quarter was not worth it.
label: decision

text: Application secrets sit in AWS Secrets Manager with rotation lambdas on a 30-day cadence and IAM-scoped access per service role.
label: architecture

text: Standardised on SOPS with age keys for all in-repo secrets instead of encrypted dotenv files scattered per service.
label: decision

text: Each repo ships a .sops.yaml declaring its age recipients and a CI job decrypts the selected file into a short-lived env at deploy time.
label: architecture

text: Moved away from the internal CA-signed certificates to ACME via Let's Encrypt after the internal CA expired unnoticed and took two regions offline.
label: decision

text: All ingress certificates are issued by cert-manager through the Let's Encrypt production issuer with HTTP-01 challenges terminated at the edge.
label: architecture

text: Kept the private PKI for workload mTLS even after moving public edges to ACME; service identity belongs to us, not a public CA.
label: decision

text: Workload identities are issued by an internal SPIFFE-compatible CA with 24-hour certificates distributed by a sidecar on every pod.
label: architecture

text: Adopted pgBackRest for Postgres backups after pg_dump slots held the WAL for hours and pushed disks to 95 percent on the primary.
label: decision

text: Each Postgres primary streams WAL to pgBackRest which writes full and differential backups to object storage with a 30-day retention window.
label: architecture

text: Decided Velero was mandatory before we let product teams run Argo apps with stateful charts in the shared cluster.
label: decision

text: Velero runs on every cluster with a daily schedule that snapshots all namespaces and ships restic payloads plus PV snapshots to a regional bucket.
label: architecture

text: Rejected a cold DR target in favour of a warm standby after tabletop exercises showed we could not meet the 1-hour RTO with a cold spin-up.
label: decision

text: DR lives in us-east-2 as a warm standby: Aurora global database replica, scaled-to-one Kubernetes deployments, and DNS weighted at 0 until failover.
label: architecture

text: Committed to active/active across two AWS regions instead of active/passive so the quarterly failover game days were no longer a fire drill.
label: decision

text: Traffic is split 50/50 between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 via Route 53 latency records with per-region Aurora writers and conflict-free replicated state.
label: architecture

text: Dropped Datadog after the annual bill crossed mid six figures and the platform team said they could run the OSS stack for a fraction of the cost.
label: decision

text: Observability runs on a self-hosted stack of Prometheus, Loki, Tempo, and Grafana with Mimir fronting long-term metric storage on S3.
label: architecture

text: Picked Honeycomb for production tracing over an internal Jaeger build; BubbleUp paid for itself in the first two incidents.
label: decision

text: Application services emit OTLP spans to a Honeycomb ingest endpoint through a regional collector that handles sampling and tail-based retention.
label: architecture

text: Replaced the Fluentd daemonsets with Fluent Bit after the Ruby footprint cost us 1 GB of RAM per node for no functional gain.
label: decision

text: Every node runs a Fluent Bit daemonset that tails container logs, enriches with Kubernetes metadata, and forwards to Loki over gRPC.
label: architecture

text: Chose Vector as the aggregation layer instead of Logstash because the config is typed and the pipeline can be unit-tested offline.
label: decision

text: Per-region Vector aggregators receive logs from edge collectors, apply VRL-based PII scrubbing, and fan out to Loki, S3, and SIEM sinks.
label: architecture

text: Switched long-term metrics from Thanos to VictoriaMetrics; Thanos store-gateway cost and query latency at our cardinality were unworkable.
label: decision

text: Metrics are scraped by vmagent, shipped to a vmcluster of three vmstorage nodes per region, and queried through vmselect behind Grafana.
label: architecture

text: Kept Prometheus at the cluster edge but remote-wrote everything into Mimir so the on-call teams never had to federate by hand again.
label: decision

text: Each cluster runs a Prometheus pair with remote_write pointed at a central Mimir deployment backed by S3 for long-term blocks.
label: architecture

text: Standardised on the OpenTelemetry Collector as the single tracing ingress instead of running vendor agents next to each application.
label: decision

text: Applications emit OTLP to a collector daemonset which batches, samples, and exports to Tempo for trace storage and to Mimir for RED metrics.
label: architecture

text: Cut Jaeger retention from 14 days to 3 after storage costs doubled in a quarter and nobody queried traces older than 48 hours.
label: decision

text: Jaeger runs with a Cassandra backend limited to 3-day TTL per span index and an archive path for flagged traces that writes to S3 for 90 days.
label: architecture

text: Retired the hand-rolled WireGuard mesh in favour of Tailscale once the ACL tooling started reviewing itself and the key distribution broke in DR.
label: decision

text: Operator access to prod flows through Tailscale with ACLs generated from the HR system and exit nodes landing in each cloud VPC.
label: architecture

text: Kept IPsec tunnels for partner B2B links even after migrating staff to Tailscale; partners require dedicated static-routed endpoints.
label: decision

text: Partner integrations terminate on two IPsec VPN gateways in us-east-1 with BGP peering into a dedicated transit VPC that hosts the exchange services.
label: architecture

text: Killed the SSH bastion fleet and switched to AWS Session Manager; key rotation and just-in-time access were both solved for free.
label: decision

text: Shell access to EC2 instances goes through AWS Session Manager with IAM roles gating which principals can start sessions on which tags.
label: architecture

text: Chose Teleport over Boundary for privileged access because the recording and RBAC model lined up cleanly with the SOC 2 audit requirements.
label: decision

text: Teleport proxies sit in a dedicated VPC and broker SSH, Kubernetes, and Postgres sessions with full session recording to an S3 bucket.
label: architecture

text: Automated the regional failover runbook after the manual procedure missed a single Terraform variable and cost us another 20 minutes.
label: decision

text: Failover is driven by a Step Functions state machine that flips Route 53 weights, promotes the Aurora replica, and drains the stale ASG in parallel.
label: architecture

text: Held the line on EU-only data storage for EU customers instead of a cheaper single-region design once GDPR legal review flagged the transfer risk.
label: decision

text: EU customer data lives in two eu-west subnets with replicated Postgres and S3 buckets, all KMS-encrypted with keys that never leave the region.
label: architecture

text: Committed to a three-year compute Savings Plan covering 70 percent of baseline EC2 usage; the finance team signed off after the first quarterly review.
label: decision

text: Baseline compute runs on reserved capacity backed by a compute Savings Plan with bursts served by on-demand and interruptible spot capacity.
label: architecture

text: Moved the batch ML fleet to spot-first after a month of checkpointing work proved interruptions were cheaper than on-demand pricing.
label: decision

text: Batch training jobs run on a Karpenter-managed spot node group with per-job checkpointing to S3 and a fallback on-demand pool for stragglers.
label: architecture

text: Rolled the fleet from gp2 to gp3 volumes once the IOPS-per-dollar math became unambiguous at any volume size above 100 GiB.
label: decision

text: All stateful workloads use gp3 volumes with baseline IOPS provisioned per workload tier and snapshot schedules managed by AWS Backup.
label: architecture

text: Stood up MinIO on the colo hardware instead of a pure cloud object store because the data residency contract required on-site copies.
label: decision

text: On-prem object storage is a four-node MinIO cluster in erasure-coded mode behind an HAProxy layer with replication to an offsite S3 bucket.
label: architecture

text: Ripped out Istio after the third control-plane upgrade broke mTLS on a Friday afternoon; Linkerd's smaller surface area was worth the feature loss.
label: decision

text: Service-to-service traffic flows through a Linkerd mesh with automatic mTLS and per-deployment traffic shift manifests driving progressive rollouts.
label: architecture

text: Chose Consul Connect over a pure Kubernetes mesh because half the workloads still run on VMs and needed the same identity fabric.
label: decision

text: VMs and pods share identity through Consul Connect; envoy sidecars are injected by Nomad or the Kubernetes webhook depending on workload type.
label: architecture

text: Replaced the nginx ingress controller with Envoy-based Contour after per-tenant rate limiting turned into a lua maintenance problem.
label: decision

text: Edge ingress runs Contour with Envoy data planes; per-tenant RateLimitPolicy CRDs feed into a global ratelimit service backed by Redis.
label: architecture

text: Consolidated three separate API gateways onto a single Kong deployment after plugin drift caused contradictory auth behaviours across teams.
label: decision

text: All north-south HTTP traffic enters a Kong gateway tier where JWT validation, mTLS enforcement, and request transformation plugins run in a fixed order.
label: architecture

text: Moved the primary transactional database from self-managed Postgres on EC2 to Aurora PostgreSQL after the on-call rota blamed failovers three quarters running.
label: decision

text: OLTP workloads run on an Aurora PostgreSQL cluster with one writer and three readers, snapshotted daily and replicated to a second region for DR.
label: architecture

text: Chose CockroachDB Dedicated over self-hosting the same binary; we wanted the distributed SQL guarantees without owning the node repair story.
label: decision

text: Ledger workloads run on CockroachDB Dedicated in a three-region configuration with survival mode set to region failure and backups to object storage.
label: architecture

text: Rejected a managed Redis in favour of self-hosted Redis Cluster once the managed per-shard pricing crossed the break-even against a small SRE rota.
label: decision

text: The shared cache tier is a six-shard Redis Cluster on dedicated nodes with TLS between primaries and replicas and Sentinel wired only for failover detection.
label: architecture

text: Kept Memcached for session storage even after moving everything else to Redis; the single-purpose simplicity kept paging incidents at zero for two years.
label: decision

text: Session data sits in a three-node Memcached fleet behind a consistent-hash client library with a TTL equal to the session cookie lifetime.
label: architecture

text: Retired the self-hosted RabbitMQ cluster in favour of SQS for general async work; quorum queue operations were eating one engineer-week per month.
label: decision

text: Async jobs flow through SQS standard queues with a separate FIFO queue for billing writes and DLQs configured for five retries before alerting.
label: architecture

text: Stuck with self-managed Kafka rather than Kinesis because exactly-once semantics with compacted topics were not achievable on the managed offering when we evaluated.
label: decision

text: Event backbone is a Kafka cluster of nine brokers per region using KRaft mode, TLS/SASL auth, and MirrorMaker 2 for cross-region topic replication.
label: architecture

text: Moved long CI pipelines from GitHub-hosted Actions to self-hosted Buildkite agents after single-job times consistently crossed the 6-hour hard limit.
label: decision

text: CI runs on a Buildkite agent fleet autoscaled on EKS with ephemeral runners per job and a shared S3-backed artifact cache keyed by dependency lockfile hashes.
label: architecture

text: Adopted ArgoCD with Argo Rollouts over the home-grown deploy script once a bad canary slipped through and took 25 percent of traffic for 9 minutes.
label: decision

text: Every service deploys via ArgoCD with Rollouts CRDs driving 5/25/50/100 percent canary steps gated on Prometheus analysis queries and manual approval at 50.
label: architecture

text: Shifted bot mitigation from an in-cluster nginx module up to Cloud Armor after a volumetric attack saturated the ingress NLB for 12 minutes.
label: decision

text: Public traffic passes a Cloud Armor policy with managed bot rules, a rate-limit rule per origin IP, and a WAF preconfigured rule set for OWASP top 10.
label: architecture

text: Dropped symptom-based CPU alerts in favour of SLO-driven alerting because two years of page data showed CPU alerts had a 6 percent precision rate.
label: decision

text: Alerting is driven by Sloth-generated SLOs; burn-rate alerts at 2 percent and 5 percent of the monthly budget page the on-call, everything else is a ticket.
label: architecture

text: Switched the event pipeline from Kinesis to Redpanda after throughput stopped keeping up with the dashboards.
label: decision

text: Events land in a Redpanda topic, feed a Flink job, and materialise into Iceberg tables partitioned by event_date.
label: architecture

text: Moved the real-time aggregations off Spark Structured Streaming onto Flink once watermark handling became too brittle.
label: decision

text: Flink jobs consume from Kafka, keyed by tenant_id, and sink rolling aggregates into a RocksDB-backed state store before emitting to a ClickHouse view.
label: architecture

text: Replaced the hand-written Airflow Bash tasks with dbt models so analytics engineers could own transformation logic.
label: decision

text: dbt runs on a Snowflake warehouse, orchestrated by Airflow's KubernetesPodOperator, with sources mapped to raw Fivetran schemas.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Apache Iceberg over plain Parquet directories because partition evolution kept breaking our backfills.
label: decision

text: Raw Parquet writes land in S3, a Glue job registers them as Iceberg tables, and Trino reads snapshots for ad-hoc analytics.
label: architecture

text: Chose BigQuery over Redshift for the new analytics surface since the workload was bursty and columnar scan costs dominated.
label: decision

text: Fivetran lands CRM data into BigQuery raw datasets, dbt materialises marts, and Looker reads from a dedicated semantic layer project.
label: architecture

text: Migrated orchestration from Airflow to Dagster after asset-centric lineage became a hard requirement for the platform team.
label: decision

text: Dagster assets define the warehouse graph, sensors poll S3 prefixes, and the daemon schedules partitioned backfills against the Snowflake target.
label: architecture

text: Picked Hightouch for reverse ETL so that go-to-market syncs stopped living in a brittle Python cron job.
label: decision

text: Hightouch reads curated marts from Snowflake and syncs them into Salesforce and HubSpot on a 15-minute cadence with diff-based upserts.
label: architecture

text: Replaced the Kafka Connect JDBC source with Debezium for Postgres CDC because logical replication slots gave us ordered change streams.
label: decision

text: Debezium reads from Postgres replication slots, publishes to Kafka topics per table, and a Flink job upserts them into an Iceberg mirror.
label: architecture

text: Introduced Confluent Schema Registry after a malformed Avro message silently corrupted a downstream mart for two days.
label: decision

text: Producers register Avro schemas against the registry, Kafka brokers enforce compatibility, and consumers resolve schema ids lazily via a local cache.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Monte Carlo for data observability since our custom freshness checks could not cover cross-schema volume anomalies.
label: decision

text: Monte Carlo agents query Snowflake INFORMATION_SCHEMA, detect freshness and volume anomalies, and post incidents into a dedicated Slack channel.
label: architecture

text: Standardised on Great Expectations over the bespoke assertion library because suites needed to be generated from JSON schemas.
label: decision

text: Great Expectations runs inside Airflow, validates Parquet batches on S3, and writes data docs back to a versioned S3 bucket.
label: architecture

text: Chose OpenLineage over the hand-maintained lineage wiki so upstream breakages would show up in pager alerts.
label: decision

text: Airflow emits OpenLineage events to a Marquez backend, dbt runs feed run-level lineage, and the UI surfaces downstream impact graphs.
label: architecture

text: Moved PII tokenisation from an in-app library to Skyflow after auditors flagged inconsistent masking across services.
label: decision

text: Skyflow stores raw PII behind a vault proxy, services persist only tokens, and detokenisation happens at a policy-gated API during fulfilment.
label: architecture

text: Tiered cold events out of Snowflake into S3 Glacier Deep Archive once query patterns showed no reads past 24 months.
label: decision

text: A nightly Dagster job exports partitions older than two years as Parquet to S3 Glacier and drops them from the warehouse with an audit row.
label: architecture

text: Replaced the bespoke SaaS ingestion scripts with Fivetran so that API schema drift stopped paging the data team.
label: decision

text: Fivetran connectors land raw tables in Snowflake, dbt sources reference them read-only, and a single orchestration DAG monitors sync cursors.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Apache Pulsar over Kafka for the cross-region bus once geo-replication and multi-tenant isolation became first-class requirements.
label: decision

text: Pulsar brokers run per region with geo-replicated namespaces, functions handle lightweight enrichment, and BookKeeper provides the durable log layer.
label: architecture

text: Rewrote the pandas transformation layer in SQL running under dbt so that analysts could own the models without touching Python.
label: decision

text: dbt models are organised into staging, intermediate, and marts layers, with exposures declared per dashboard and tests on every primary key.
label: architecture

text: Split the shared Snowflake warehouse into per-team virtual warehouses after noisy-neighbour pipelines starved the finance dashboards.
label: decision

text: Each team owns a dedicated virtual warehouse sized by workload, a resource monitor caps credits monthly, and queries route via role-based grants.
label: architecture

text: Replaced Hive-on-MR with Trino for interactive queries over the lake once analysts started abandoning queries at the 5-minute mark.
label: decision

text: Trino coordinators run on Kubernetes, workers autoscale on CPU pressure, and the Iceberg connector points at a shared Glue metastore.
label: architecture

text: Dropped CSV as the landing format in favour of Parquet after repeated quoting bugs corrupted downstream joins.
label: decision

text: Producers write Snappy-compressed Parquet to S3 with hourly prefixes, a Glue crawler registers the tables, and Athena exposes them for ad-hoc queries.
label: architecture

text: Swapped the legacy cron scheduler for Prefect so that retries and notifications stopped being copy-pasted into every script.
label: decision

text: Prefect flows run in an agent pool on ECS, use a Postgres backend for state, and register with a shared work queue per environment.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Hex for analyst-authored pipelines so that notebooks graduated into versioned, scheduled artifacts without a full rewrite.
label: decision

text: Hex projects connect to Snowflake via OAuth, publish scheduled runs, and expose parameterised apps that hand off heavy queries to dbt exposures.
label: architecture

text: Moved to customer-managed KMS keys for all warehouse object storage after a compliance review flagged tenant-level blast radius concerns.
label: decision

text: Each tenant's S3 prefix is encrypted with a dedicated KMS key, Snowflake external tables reference the key id, and revocation happens through a platform API.
label: architecture

text: Switched event payloads from ad-hoc JSON to Protobuf once producer-consumer drift became the most common data incident.
label: decision

text: Protobuf descriptors live in a versioned monorepo, a CI job publishes them to the schema registry, and Flink consumers resolve schemas by fingerprint.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Trino federation instead of nightly ETL copies between warehouses once product analytics needed joins across Postgres and the lake.
label: decision

text: Trino exposes a single SQL surface that federates Postgres, MySQL, Iceberg, and Elasticsearch connectors behind a shared catalog namespace.
label: architecture

text: Replaced the home-grown webhook buffer service with API Gateway plus Kinesis Firehose once traffic spikes overwhelmed its Redis queue.
label: decision

text: API Gateway authenticates webhooks, Firehose buffers events for up to 60 seconds, and a Lambda transforms them into Parquet before landing on S3.
label: architecture

text: Moved streaming SQL workloads off ksqlDB onto Flink SQL after state store corruption recurred on the 0.29 release.
label: decision

text: Flink SQL jobs run on a session cluster, checkpoint to S3 every 30 seconds, and register sinks through the Hive catalog for cross-tool discovery.
label: architecture

text: Retired Teradata for Databricks SQL once hardware refresh costs crossed the three-year Databricks commit.
label: decision

text: Databricks workspaces host Unity Catalog, Delta Lake tables sit on ADLS Gen2, and SQL warehouses serve BI tools behind a Unity-governed metastore.
label: architecture

text: Chose Flyte over Argo Workflows for ML pipelines because typed interfaces and cached artifacts mattered more than generic container DAGs.
label: decision

text: Flyte executions run on a Kubernetes cluster, artifacts persist in an S3-backed data catalog, and task caching keys off input hashes and container digests.
label: architecture

text: Switched the reverse ETL vendor from Census to Hightouch after their audience-builder better matched the marketing team's workflow.
label: decision

text: Hightouch models resolve against Snowflake marts, audiences sync incrementally into Braze and Iterable, and observability flows into the existing Datadog account.
label: architecture

text: Replaced Maxwell with Debezium for MySQL CDC once we needed transactional metadata and ordered schema change events.
label: decision

text: Debezium tails MySQL binlogs, emits events to Kafka topics keyed by primary key, and a downstream Kafka Streams job materialises a compacted changelog.
label: architecture

text: Swapped Confluent Schema Registry for Apicurio after the self-hosted license model no longer matched the platform budget.
label: decision

text: Apicurio runs behind an internal gateway, stores artifacts in Postgres, and integrates with the Kafka connect cluster via the standard Avro serde.
label: architecture

text: Added Soda Core for SQL-based data checks once shallow freshness alerts kept missing row-level quality regressions.
label: decision

text: Soda scans run as post-task steps in Airflow, write check results to a Postgres metadata store, and raise PagerDuty incidents on critical failures.
label: architecture

text: Moved away from Deequ to Great Expectations once analysts without Scala experience needed to author and review checks.
label: decision

text: Great Expectations runs on a dedicated Kubernetes deployment, stores validation results in S3, and renders data docs behind an SSO-protected static site.
label: architecture

text: Chose OpenMetadata over Datahub for the lineage catalog because the bundled profiler and governance workflow covered a wider surface.
label: decision

text: OpenMetadata ingests Airflow, dbt, Snowflake, and Kafka metadata on a schedule, and exposes a GraphQL API that the platform UI embeds for search.
label: architecture

text: Adopted a central retention service for the lake after legal teams rejected per-dataset manual purging policies.
label: decision

text: The retention service reads dataset policies from a YAML registry, issues Iceberg delete queries per partition age, and writes audit rows into a compliance bucket.
label: architecture

text: Replaced Snowflake time-travel as the long-term archival story with scheduled Parquet exports to keep compliance snapshots vendor-neutral.
label: decision

text: A weekly Dagster job exports Snowflake tables as Parquet into a versioned S3 bucket, registers them as Iceberg metadata, and tags the run with a GDPR scope.
label: architecture

text: Replaced the home-grown HTTP event collector with Segment once mobile SDK work threatened to overflow the product engineering roadmap.
label: decision

text: Segment sources land client events into Snowflake via a managed warehouse destination, with PII filters applied via protocols before warehouse delivery.
label: architecture

text: Picked Apache Beam over Spark Streaming for the cross-runner pipelines so the same code could run on Dataflow and Flink.
label: decision

text: Beam pipelines run on Google Dataflow in production and Flink locally, with side inputs backed by a BigQuery reference table refreshed hourly.
label: architecture

text: Rewrote the heavy transformation scripts from Pandas to Polars after memory spikes crashed the ECS tasks on month-end runs.
label: decision

text: Polars jobs stream Parquet batches from S3, group aggregations in a lazy plan, and write results back as partitioned Parquet for downstream dbt models.
label: architecture

text: Moved reporting workloads off a MySQL read replica onto ClickHouse once dashboard queries started timing out at p95.
label: decision

text: ClickHouse runs a sharded cluster behind a chproxy layer, ingests events via Kafka engine tables, and serves BI tools through materialised view projections.
label: architecture

text: Retired the remaining Luigi DAGs for Airflow 2 once dependency resolution and dynamic task mapping became platform-wide requirements.
label: decision

text: Airflow 2 runs on CeleryExecutor with Redis, DAGs live in a git-sync sidecar, and the scheduler uses a highly available Postgres metadata database.
label: architecture

text: Swapped the Zapier glue for Workato after ops workflows started needing multi-step error handling and audit logs.
label: decision

text: Workato recipes pull curated marts from Snowflake, fan out to Salesforce, NetSuite, and Slack, and log every step into a central recipe audit table.
label: architecture

text: Replaced the Airbyte Postgres source with Debezium once batch-based CDC could no longer meet the 30-second freshness SLA.
label: decision

text: Debezium runs on a Kafka Connect cluster, publishes row-level changes to Kafka, and a Spark Structured Streaming job applies them to Delta tables.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Buf Schema Registry for Protobuf sharing after manual vendored copies drifted across five repos in one quarter.
label: decision

text: Buf hosts the canonical Protobuf modules, CI checks enforce breaking-change policies, and code generation fans out into Go, Python, and TypeScript clients.
label: architecture

text: Moved the data platform's pipeline logs from Datadog to a dedicated Grafana Loki stack because indexed log cost outgrew the per-month budget.
label: decision

text: Promtail ships pipeline logs to Loki, Grafana dashboards correlate with Prometheus pipeline metrics, and alerts route through a Grafana OnCall schedule.
label: architecture

text: Committed to dbt tests as the minimum bar for every new mart after a silent dimension break caused a reporting-day incident.
label: decision

text: Every dbt model carries not-null and unique tests on its primary key, plus referential tests on foreign keys, gated by a CI check on pull requests.
label: architecture

text: Replaced Apache Atlas with Marquez for lineage once the Hadoop-centric data model stopped matching our warehouse-first pipelines.
label: decision

text: Marquez stores OpenLineage events in Postgres, exposes a REST API for consumers, and a custom UI overlay surfaces column-level lineage for dbt models.
label: architecture

text: Built a dedicated subject-request service so that GDPR deletions stopped going through ad-hoc SQL scripts touching every warehouse table.
label: decision

text: The subject-request service reads a data map from a catalog, issues tombstone rows into Iceberg tables, and records per-request proofs in a tamper-evident log.
label: architecture

text: Chose a lakehouse-only archival strategy over cross-region warehouse replicas to avoid doubling the Snowflake storage spend.
label: decision

text: Cold partitions live as Iceberg tables on S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval, a Unity Catalog external location governs access, and Databricks SQL reads them on demand.
label: architecture

text: Moved from long-lived API keys to short-lived JWTs after the 2026-01 key leak forced a fleet-wide rotation.
label: decision

text: Every service accepts only RS256-signed JWTs with a 10-minute TTL; signing keys rotate nightly from the step-ca issuer.
label: architecture

text: Retired the hand-rolled KMS wrapper in favour of Vault Transit; custody and audit requirements outgrew the in-house code.
label: decision

text: Vault Transit holds every application data key behind AppRole auth; services call encrypt/decrypt endpoints and never see raw key material.
label: architecture

text: Switched from manual Let's Encrypt renewals to cert-manager after a missed renewal caused a 40-minute outage in February.
label: decision

text: cert-manager reconciles Certificate CRs in every namespace, renews 30 days before expiry, and mounts the result as a TLS secret on each pod.
label: architecture

text: Dropped plaintext secrets in CI environment variables and adopted Vault dynamic database credentials after a log leak exposed a static password.
label: decision

text: CI jobs pull ephemeral database roles from Vault at runtime with a 15-minute TTL; static credentials are banned by a repo-level policy check.
label: architecture

text: Abandoned the flat production VPC and rolled out Cilium network policies after a compromised pod reached the billing subnet laterally.
label: decision

text: Cilium enforces default-deny egress in every namespace; allowed flows are declared per service via CiliumNetworkPolicy and tested in CI.
label: architecture

text: Replaced the AWS managed WAF ruleset with Coraza running the OWASP Core Rule Set; we needed tunable anomaly thresholds the managed one did not expose.
label: decision

text: Coraza sits in front of the ingress gateway with CRS 4.0 in blocking mode above an anomaly score of 10; matched requests are tagged and streamed to Loki.
label: architecture

text: Migrated the perimeter IDS from Snort to Suricata after the Snort rule feed stopped covering our TLS 1.3 traffic patterns.
label: decision

text: Suricata runs inline on the north-south edge, consumes the ET Pro ruleset, and drops traffic that matches the `dropable` tag; events go to Elastic.
label: architecture

text: Split security audit events out of the generic log pipeline after auditors flagged that we could mutate them post-hoc.
label: decision

text: Security audit events ship to an append-only Loki tenant with object-lock retention of 7 years; the write role cannot delete or overwrite.
label: architecture

text: Dropped the nested role hierarchy we had in the admin app and moved to OPA-based attribute checks; the role tree had become impossible to reason about.
label: decision

text: The admin backend calls an OPA sidecar on every request; policies are rego files in git, tested with opa test, and evaluated against user attributes plus resource tags.
label: architecture

text: Retired the corporate VPN for internal tooling after a stolen laptop exposed the shared CIDR; went with an identity-aware proxy instead.
label: decision

text: All internal web tools sit behind Pomerium; device posture and SSO identity are evaluated per request and the underlying services only accept traffic from the proxy's mTLS cert.
label: architecture

text: Replaced the manual device allowlist with TPM-based attestation; operators were sharing device certificates and we could not tell which laptop signed what.
label: decision

text: Every workstation enrolls its TPM EK into smallstep; access tokens are only minted after a fresh attestation quote signs a recent nonce from the issuer.
label: architecture

text: Started signing every internal binary with cosign after a build-server compromise shipped a backdoored CLI to staging.
label: decision

text: Release pipelines sign artifacts with keyless cosign using the OIDC token of the GitHub Actions job; verification runs as an admission controller on every cluster.
label: architecture

text: Version pinning was not enough after the event-stream incident, so we adopted SLSA level 3 provenance for every first-party and vendored dependency.
label: decision

text: Build provenance is emitted by the Tekton chain, stored in Rekor, and verified at deploy time; images without a matching in-toto attestation are rejected by the admission webhook.
label: architecture

text: Nightly-only Trivy scans let a critical CVE sit in production for 14 hours, so we added inline scanning on every push.
label: decision

text: Trivy runs in the PR pipeline against the built image and again as a nightly sweep against every running workload; criticals block the merge and page the on-call.
label: architecture

text: Adopted PagerDuty incident workflows after the December outage ran for two hours with nobody declaring commander.
label: decision

text: Every severity-1 page opens a PagerDuty incident channel, assigns a commander from the on-call rotation, and links the standard security-incident runbook automatically.
label: architecture

text: Host-level LUKS was not enough to satisfy the new PII contract, so we moved to application-layer envelope encryption for customer records.
label: decision

text: Each customer record is encrypted with a per-tenant data key; data keys are wrapped by a Vault Transit master key and stored alongside the ciphertext in Postgres.
label: architecture

text: Moved from opportunistic TLS to mandatory mTLS on every east-west hop after packet captures showed a test service still speaking plaintext in prod.
label: decision

text: Istio sidecars enforce strict mTLS on every pod-to-pod connection; the mesh refuses plaintext and certificates come from a short-lived SPIFFE issuer.
label: architecture

text: Long-lived server sessions were causing replay problems after stolen cookies, so we moved to short access tokens with rotating refresh.
label: decision

text: Web clients hold a 10-minute access token and a 24-hour refresh token; the refresh endpoint rotates both on every call and revokes the family on reuse detection.
label: architecture

text: Killed the local admin account table in favour of Okta SSO after we found three shared logins still in use six months after onboarding Okta.
label: decision

text: All internal tools authenticate against Okta via OIDC; group claims drive role mapping and the local account path is disabled at the application level.
label: architecture

text: Upgraded the password hash from bcrypt at cost 10 to argon2id after the 2026-Q1 GPU cracking benchmark showed bcrypt falling behind.
label: decision

text: Argon2id runs with m=64MB, t=3, p=4 inside the auth service; hashes are versioned and re-computed on successful login for users still on the old bcrypt scheme.
label: architecture

text: The in-house rate limiter collapsed under a 300 Gbps SYN flood in November, so we moved edge DDoS defence to Cloudflare Magic Transit.
label: decision

text: Cloudflare Magic Transit announces our /24 and scrubs traffic before forwarding over GRE to the origin routers; the in-house limiter now only handles layer 7 quotas.
label: architecture

text: Distroless images alone were not enough after a container escape attempt via /tmp, so we tightened the runtime profile as well.
label: decision

text: Production pods run as non-root with a read-only root filesystem, drop every Linux capability, and use the `runtime/default` seccomp profile enforced by Kyverno.
label: architecture

text: Plain UDP DNS inside the VPC exposed us to cache poisoning scenarios, so we switched to DoT with DNSSEC validation on the resolver tier.
label: decision

text: Unbound resolvers in every region do DNSSEC validation and forward upstream over DoT to 1.1.1.1; workloads hit the resolvers over an internal Anycast VIP.
label: architecture

text: The shared-bearer pattern at the API gateway let one partner's leaked token hit other tenants, so we moved to OAuth 2.1 with audience binding.
label: decision

text: Kong at the edge validates the JWT signature, checks the `aud` claim against the matched route, and injects a per-tenant identity header that downstream services trust only from the gateway's mTLS peer.
label: architecture

text: Dropped static service account tokens after one leaked in a core dump; SPIFFE gave us short-lived, workload-bound identities instead.
label: decision

text: SPIRE agents attest each workload via the Kubernetes PSAT selector and issue SVIDs with a 1-hour TTL; gRPC servers authenticate peers by SPIFFE ID, not token.
label: architecture

text: The shared `app` Postgres role made postmortems impossible, so we moved to Vault-issued per-request database roles.
label: decision

text: Every request path opens a Postgres connection with a Vault-issued role scoped to the tenant and lifecycle; role grants are generated from the OPA policy bundle at deploy time.
label: architecture

text: SPF alone kept letting lookalike domains through, so we added DKIM signing and pushed DMARC to p=reject after a full quarter on quarantine.
label: decision

text: Outbound mail is signed with a rotating 2048-bit DKIM key per brand domain; DMARC is published at p=reject with aggregate reports piped into a weekly review dashboard.
label: architecture

text: Cleartext restic repositories on S3 scared the new CISO, so we wrapped every backup with age and kept the key offline.
label: decision

text: Backups are written to an S3 bucket with object-lock; restic chunks are encrypted with age using a recipient key whose private half lives only on two offline YubiKeys in the safe.
label: architecture

text: The iOS team stopped shipping debuggable builds and added Play Integrity / App Attest checks after a reverse-engineered APK hit a test forum.
label: decision

text: Release builds pin the API certificate, require a valid App Attest or Play Integrity token on every sensitive call, and refuse to run under a debugger in production flavour.
label: architecture

text: The 2025 crypto-miner incident got in through an allow-by-default egress rule, so we flipped production to default-deny with an explicit allow-list.
label: decision

text: Calico GlobalNetworkPolicies deny all egress in production by default; required destinations are declared per workload and reviewed quarterly against traffic logs.
label: architecture

text: Admin TOTP was phished twice in six months, so we went passwordless with WebAuthn for anyone with production access.
label: decision

text: Admin logins require a WebAuthn assertion from a resident key on a FIDO2 authenticator; password and TOTP paths are disabled for users in the `admins` group at the IdP.
label: architecture

text: Pulling base images directly from Docker Hub bit us during a rate-limit outage and again with a typosquatted tag, so we routed everything through an internal Harbor proxy.
label: decision

text: Harbor proxies Docker Hub and GHCR with on-pull Trivy scanning and cosign signature verification; the cluster's containerd only trusts `registry.corp/*` and refuses other registries.
label: architecture

text: The legacy `unsafe-inline` CSP let a reflected XSS reach session cookies, so we moved the web app to a strict nonce-based policy.
label: decision

text: Every HTML response sets a CSP with `script-src 'self' 'nonce-<per-request>'` and `strict-dynamic`; violations stream to a report-uri endpoint that alerts on novel hashes.
label: architecture

text: Long-lived SSH keys kept showing up on ex-employee laptops, so we cut over to short-lived SSH certificates signed by Teleport.
label: decision

text: Teleport's CA signs SSH certificates valid for 8 hours after SSO + MFA; servers trust only the Teleport CA and the `authorized_keys` path is disabled in sshd_config.
label: architecture

text: Post-hoc grep sweeps kept missing leaked PII, so we moved redaction up to the logger itself before anything hits disk.
label: decision

text: The shared logging wrapper runs a redaction pass on every record using typed field tags; fields marked `sensitive` are hashed with a rotating salt before the log line is serialised.
label: architecture

text: Running the admin plane next to workloads meant one compromised node could reach the CI controller, so we split it onto a dedicated management cluster.
label: decision

text: Admin tools (ArgoCD, Vault, Teleport) run on a separate hardened cluster reachable only via the identity-aware proxy; workload clusters pull from the admin cluster and never push.
label: architecture

text: Permanent vendor VPN accounts kept outliving their support engagements, so we moved third-party access to a just-in-time broker.
label: decision

text: Vendors request time-boxed access through the access broker; on approval, Teleport issues a 4-hour certificate scoped to the specific host and role, and the session is recorded.
label: architecture

text: Manual PR review for new dependencies missed a GPL library and a known-vulnerable transitive, so we gated it on automated checks.
label: decision

text: Every PR that changes a lockfile runs a dependency-review job that fails on GPL/AGPL imports and on advisories above High severity; overrides require a `security-approved` label from the platform team.
label: architecture

text: Pre-commit secret scanning missed commits from contractors without the hook installed, so we added server-side scanning and a weekly history sweep.
label: decision

text: gitleaks runs as a pre-receive hook on the Gitea server and as a nightly full-history sweep; detected secrets auto-open a revocation ticket and block the push.
label: architecture

text: Rotated out the last long-lived AWS IAM user keys after one leaked via a screenshare; switched CI to OIDC federation instead.
label: decision

text: GitHub Actions assumes an AWS role via OIDC with a trust policy bound to the specific repo, branch and environment; the role's session is 1 hour and scoped to a single account.
label: architecture

text: Wildcard `*:*` policies on legacy services kept surviving reviews, so we enforced permissions boundaries on every role.
label: decision

text: Every IAM role in production is attached to a permissions boundary generated from the service's declared needs; Terraform refuses to plan a role without a matching boundary file.
label: architecture

text: Shared self-hosted runners leaked caches between jobs; a poisoned cache hit the auth service build, so we moved to ephemeral per-job runners.
label: decision

text: Each GitHub Actions job spawns a fresh Firecracker microVM via the runner controller; the VM is destroyed at job end and secrets are mounted via short-lived Vault tokens.
label: architecture

text: An engineer forgot the shared-secret check in a new webhook handler, so we moved verification into a middleware that every handler must pass through.
label: decision

text: Inbound webhooks hit a single router that validates the HMAC signature and timestamp window before dispatching to the typed handler; handlers cannot be registered without declaring an allowed signer.
label: architecture

text: A 30-day manual patch cycle left hosts exposed to a kernel CVE for three weeks, so we moved to continuous automated patching with a canary ring.
label: decision

text: Kured drains and reboots nodes within 24 hours of a new kernel package; patches roll through canary, staging and production rings with health gates between each step.
label: architecture

text: Always-on root access for SRE made SOC 2 reviewers unhappy and caused one real incident, so we introduced a brokered break-glass flow.
label: decision

text: Break-glass elevation is requested via the access broker, requires a peer approval in Slack, issues a 60-minute certificate tied to a ticket, and streams the session to an immutable recording bucket.
label: architecture

text: SameSite=Lax plus a two-week session cookie let a CSRF variant through in staging, so we tightened the cookie policy for the main app.
label: decision

text: Session cookies use the `__Host-` prefix with `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict` and a 12-hour expiry; the auth service rejects any request whose cookie fails the prefix invariants.
label: architecture

text: An annual external pentest missed a staging leak that lived for eight months, so we moved to a quarterly cadence plus continuous attack surface monitoring.
label: decision

text: Pentests run quarterly with a rotating vendor; between engagements, an external attack-surface tool scans all known domains daily and files findings directly into the security tracker.
label: architecture

text: Generic annual training did not move the click rate, so we replaced it with a simulated phishing program tied to just-in-time coaching.
label: decision

text: Monthly phishing simulations target all staff; clicks trigger a 10-minute training module immediately and feed a dashboard that drives targeted follow-ups for repeat clickers.
label: architecture

text: Implicit data classification led to PII ending up in analytics datasets, so we made classification explicit and enforced it through tags.
label: decision

text: Every column in the warehouse carries a `classification` tag (public, internal, confidential, restricted); access policies, masking and retention are generated from those tags at deploy time.
label: architecture

text: Producing SBOMs only for compliance requests meant we could not answer the log4shell question quickly, so we started generating them on every build.
label: decision

text: Every build writes a CycloneDX SBOM to the artifact store; a nightly job diffs each SBOM against the previous tag and opens a ticket for any dependency whose advisories changed.
label: architecture

text: A moral agent ought to act only on maxims that the agent can consistently will to hold as universal laws binding on every rational being.
label: fact

text: John Rawls, A Theory of Justice (Harvard University Press, 1971), argues that principles of justice are those that would be chosen by rational parties behind a veil of ignorance in the original position.
label: reference

text: Fair principles of social justice are the principles that rational people would agree to if they had to choose without knowing their own social position, talents, or conception of the good.
label: fact

text: Derek Parfit, Reasons and Persons (Oxford University Press, 1984), argues that personal identity over time consists in psychological continuity and connectedness rather than in a further fact about a persisting self.
label: reference

text: The persistence of a person over time is constituted by overlapping chains of memory, intention, and psychological connection rather than by any extra metaphysical fact about a continuing self.
label: fact

text: G. E. M. Anscombe, 'Modern Moral Philosophy', Philosophy 33 (1958) 1-19, argues that the concepts of moral obligation and moral duty should be jettisoned until an adequate philosophy of psychology is available.
label: reference

text: The modern vocabulary of moral obligation and moral duty makes little sense outside a theological framework, and ethics should be rebuilt on a theory of human flourishing and the virtues.
label: fact

text: Edmund Gettier, 'Is Justified True Belief Knowledge?', Analysis 23 (1963) 121-123, presents counterexamples showing that justified true belief is insufficient for knowledge.
label: reference

text: A person can have a justified true belief without having knowledge, because the belief can be true only by accident relative to its justification.
label: fact

text: Thomas Nagel, 'What Is It Like to Be a Bat?', The Philosophical Review 83 (1974) 435-450, argues that consciousness has an essentially subjective character that escapes any objective physicalist reduction.
label: reference

text: Conscious experience has an irreducibly subjective character, and no purely objective description of neural or physical processes can fully capture what it is like to be a conscious subject.
label: fact

text: David Chalmers, 'Facing Up to the Problem of Consciousness', Journal of Consciousness Studies 2 (1995) 200-219, distinguishes the easy problems of cognition from the hard problem of explaining phenomenal experience.
