text: Model studies indicate stratospheric aerosol injection could partially offset surface warming, but would also disrupt regional precipitation patterns and monsoon systems.
label: fact

text: WRI Aqueduct 4.0 (2023) estimates that 25 countries, home to a quarter of the world's population, face extremely high water stress, with withdrawals exceeding 80 percent of renewable supply.
label: reference

text: About a quarter of the world's population lives in 25 countries where water withdrawals exceed 80 percent of renewable supply, classified as extremely high water stress.
label: fact

text: Hugonnet et al., Nature 592 (2021) 726-731, used satellite stereo imagery to estimate that glaciers outside the ice sheets lost 267 gigatonnes per year between 2000 and 2019, contributing 0.74 millimetres per year to sea level rise.
label: reference

text: Mountain glaciers outside the great ice sheets lost mass at about 267 gigatonnes per year over 2000 to 2019, adding roughly 0.7 millimetres per year to global sea level.
label: fact

text: Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service press release (2023) reported that Canadian wildfires released about 480 megatonnes of carbon in 2023, more than double the previous annual record for the country.
label: reference

text: The 2023 Canadian wildfire season released roughly 480 megatonnes of carbon, more than double any previous year on record for the country.
label: fact

text: The European Commission Joint Research Centre report, 'Drought in Europe August 2022' (JRC130738, 2022), concluded that 47 percent of the territory of the European Union was under drought warning conditions in August 2022, the worst in at least 500 years.
label: reference

text: Nearly half of the European Union faced drought warning conditions in August 2022, making it the continent's worst drought in at least five centuries.
label: fact

text: Donato et al., Nature Geoscience 4 (2011) 293-297, showed that mangroves store 1023 megagrams of carbon per hectare on average, among the most carbon-rich forests in the tropics.
label: reference

text: Mangrove forests store on the order of 1000 tonnes of carbon per hectare, making them one of the most carbon-dense ecosystems in the tropics.
label: fact

text: Rockstrom et al., Nature 461 (2009) 472-475, identified the anthropogenic nitrogen fixation rate of about 121 teragrams per year as exceeding the proposed planetary boundary of 35 teragrams per year.
label: reference

text: Humans fix reactive nitrogen at roughly three times the rate considered safe for ecosystems, driving widespread eutrophication and pollution of waterways.
label: fact

text: Rignot et al., Science 341 (2013) 266-270, used satellite data to estimate that Antarctic ice-shelf basal melting accounts for 1325 gigatonnes per year, exceeding iceberg calving as the main mass-loss process.
label: reference

text: Basal melting beneath Antarctic ice shelves now removes more ice per year than iceberg calving, with a combined loss of over 1300 gigatonnes annually.
label: fact

text: Pistone, Eisenman, and Ramanathan, PNAS 111 (2014) 3322-3326, used CERES satellite data to estimate that loss of Arctic sea ice from 1979 to 2011 caused a globally averaged radiative forcing of 0.21 watts per square metre.
label: reference

text: Loss of reflective Arctic sea ice since 1979 has added about 0.2 watts per square metre to Earth's energy imbalance, amplifying greenhouse-gas warming.
label: fact

text: NOAA Climate Prediction Center diagnostics and the ECMWF SEAS5 seasonal forecasts indicated in mid-2023 that a strong El Nino event had developed in the tropical Pacific, consistent with widespread warm and dry anomalies across many regions.
label: reference

text: A strong El Nino event developed in the tropical Pacific during 2023, driving warm and dry anomalies across many regions of the world.
label: fact

text: The Kyoto Protocol to the UNFCCC (1997), Annex B, set binding quantified emission-limitation commitments for industrialised countries, averaging a 5 percent reduction below 1990 levels over 2008 to 2012.
label: reference

text: The Kyoto Protocol bound industrialised countries to reduce their greenhouse-gas emissions by an average of 5 percent below 1990 levels during 2008 to 2012.
label: fact

text: Stanley Milgram, 'Behavioral Study of Obedience', Journal of Abnormal and Social Psychology 67 (1963) 371-378, reported that 65 percent of adult participants continued to deliver what they believed were increasingly severe electric shocks to a confederate at the instruction of an experimenter.
label: reference

text: Under direct instruction from a perceived authority figure, a large majority of ordinary adults are willing to administer what they believe are dangerous electric shocks to another person.
label: fact

text: Bandura, Ross, and Ross, 'Transmission of Aggression through Imitation of Aggressive Models', Journal of Abnormal and Social Psychology 63 (1961) 575-582, showed that children who observed an adult model attack a Bobo doll later reproduced the same aggressive behaviour more often than control children.
label: reference

text: Young children who watch adults behave aggressively toward an inflatable doll are substantially more likely to imitate that aggression themselves when given the opportunity.
label: fact

text: Baumeister and Leary, 'The Need to Belong: Desire for Interpersonal Attachments as a Fundamental Human Motivation', Psychological Bulletin 117 (1995) 497-529, argued that the need for stable, caring social bonds is a pervasive and fundamental human motive with broad cognitive, emotional, and health consequences.
label: reference

text: The drive to form and maintain lasting interpersonal bonds is a basic human motivation, and persistent failure to satisfy it is linked to poorer mental and physical health outcomes.
label: fact

text: Tversky and Kahneman, 'Judgment under Uncertainty: Heuristics and Biases', Science 185 (1974) 1124-1131, described how people rely on a small number of cognitive heuristics - representativeness, availability, and anchoring - that produce systematic deviations from normative probability judgments.
label: reference

text: When estimating probabilities people rely on mental shortcuts such as how typical an example seems, how easily instances come to mind, and whichever number was suggested first, leading to predictable biases.
label: fact

text: Kahneman and Tversky, 'Prospect Theory: An Analysis of Decision under Risk', Econometrica 47 (1979) 263-292, introduced a model in which people evaluate outcomes as gains or losses from a reference point and are roughly twice as sensitive to losses as to equivalent gains.
label: reference

text: People evaluate risky outcomes relative to a reference point rather than in terms of final wealth, and a loss of a given size generally feels about twice as intense as a gain of the same size.
label: fact

text: Solomon Asch, 'Studies of Independence and Conformity: A Minority of One Against a Unanimous Majority', Psychological Monographs 70 (1956), reported that about one-third of participants conformed to a unanimous but clearly incorrect group judgment on a simple line-matching task.
label: reference

text: When a unanimous group gives an obviously wrong answer on a simple perceptual task, a substantial fraction of individuals will publicly agree with the group rather than report what they actually see.
label: fact

text: Festinger and Carlsmith, 'Cognitive Consequences of Forced Compliance', Journal of Abnormal and Social Psychology 58 (1959) 203-210, found that participants paid only one dollar to describe a boring task as enjoyable later rated the task more favorably than those paid twenty dollars.
label: reference

text: People who are induced to publicly endorse a position for a small reward later come to hold that position more sincerely than people paid a large reward for the same endorsement.
label: fact

text: Haney, Banks, and Zimbardo, 'Interpersonal Dynamics in a Simulated Prison', International Journal of Criminology and Penology 1 (1973) 69-97, reported that college students randomly assigned to guard and prisoner roles rapidly adopted abusive and submissive behaviour, forcing early termination of the study.
label: reference

text: Assigning ordinary people to strong social roles such as guard and prisoner in a simulated institution can rapidly produce coercive behaviour on one side and submission on the other.
label: fact

text: David Rosenhan, 'On Being Sane in Insane Places', Science 179 (1973) 250-258, described how pseudopatients who briefly feigned a single symptom were admitted to psychiatric hospitals and then diagnosed as mentally ill despite subsequently behaving normally.
label: reference

text: Once people are labelled as psychiatric patients, staff in mental hospitals tend to reinterpret their normal behaviour through the lens of the diagnosis and have difficulty recognising them as sane.
label: fact

text: Ainsworth, Blehar, Waters, and Wall, Patterns of Attachment (Lawrence Erlbaum, 1978), introduced the Strange Situation procedure and classified infant-caregiver attachment as secure, anxious-resistant, or anxious-avoidant.
label: reference

text: Infants' responses to brief separation from and reunion with a caregiver fall into recognisable attachment patterns, including secure, anxious-resistant, and anxious-avoidant styles.
label: fact

text: Jean Piaget, The Child's Conception of Number (Routledge and Kegan Paul, 1952), documented that children below about seven years typically fail conservation-of-number tasks in which physical rearrangement changes perceived quantity.
label: reference

text: Young children under roughly seven years of age often judge that the number of objects has changed when the objects are simply spread out or rearranged in space.
label: fact

text: Harry Harlow, 'The Nature of Love', American Psychologist 13 (1958) 673-685, reported that infant rhesus monkeys strongly preferred a cloth surrogate mother that provided contact comfort over a wire surrogate that provided food.
label: reference

text: Infant monkeys separated from their mothers prefer a soft cloth-covered surrogate that offers contact comfort over a wire surrogate that only provides food.
label: fact

text: Seligman and Maier, 'Failure to Escape Traumatic Shock', Journal of Experimental Psychology 74 (1967) 1-9, showed that dogs exposed to inescapable shock later failed to escape or avoid shocks they could control, a phenomenon termed learned helplessness.
label: reference

text: Animals and humans repeatedly exposed to aversive events they cannot control tend to stop trying to escape such events even when escape later becomes possible.
label: fact

text: Aaron Beck, 'Thinking and Depression: Idiosyncratic Content and Cognitive Distortions', Archives of General Psychiatry 9 (1963) 324-333, proposed that depression is maintained by systematic negative distortions in automatic thoughts about the self, the world, and the future.
label: reference

text: Depression is sustained in part by systematic negative biases in how people think about themselves, their circumstances, and their future prospects.
label: fact

text: Costa and McCrae, 'Four Ways Five Factors are Basic', Personality and Individual Differences 13 (1992) 653-665, consolidated evidence that personality variation in adults is well described by five broad dimensions: openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, and neuroticism.
label: reference

text: Individual differences in adult personality are largely captured by five broad trait dimensions commonly labelled openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, and neuroticism.
label: fact

text: Mischel, Shoda, and Rodriguez, 'Delay of Gratification in Children', Science 244 (1989) 933-938, summarized longitudinal follow-ups of preschool children who waited longer in the marshmallow paradigm and later showed better adolescent cognitive and social competence.
label: reference

text: Preschool children who can wait longer for a larger delayed reward tend on average to show somewhat better cognitive and social outcomes in adolescence.
label: fact

text: Carol Dweck, Mindset: The New Psychology of Success (Random House, 2006), synthesized research showing that students who believe intelligence is malleable tend to seek challenge and persist after failure more than those who view intelligence as fixed.
label: reference

text: Students who believe that intelligence can grow with effort tend to embrace challenging work and recover from setbacks better than students who see intelligence as an unchangeable trait.
label: fact

text: Thaler and Sunstein, Nudge: Improving Decisions about Health, Wealth, and Happiness (Yale University Press, 2008), argued that small changes in choice architecture, such as default options, can predictably alter behaviour without restricting freedom of choice.
label: reference

text: Changing the default option in a decision, such as whether employees are automatically enrolled in a savings plan, can substantially shift participation rates without removing anyone's ability to opt out.
label: fact

text: Mazar, Amir, and Ariely, 'The Dishonesty of Honest People: A Theory of Self-Concept Maintenance', Journal of Marketing Research 45 (2008) 633-644, reported that many participants cheat by small amounts on anonymous tasks but refrain from large cheating that would threaten their self-image as honest.
label: reference

text: When given an opportunity to cheat without detection, many otherwise honest people cheat by small amounts but stop short of cheating enough to seriously threaten their view of themselves as good people.
label: fact

text: Klein et al., 'Investigating Variation in Replicability: A Many Labs Replication Project', Social Psychology 45 (2014) 142-152, coordinated 36 independent labs to replicate 13 classic findings and found that roughly ten of the effects reproduced while others did not.
label: reference

text: Large coordinated replication efforts have shown that many but not all classic social psychology findings reliably reproduce across samples and laboratories.
label: fact

text: Open Science Collaboration, 'Estimating the Reproducibility of Psychological Science', Science 349 (2015) aac4716, replicated 100 published psychology studies and found that only about 36 percent yielded statistically significant results in the same direction.
label: reference

text: In a large replication project covering a hundred published psychology studies, only a little over a third reproduced the original statistically significant finding.
label: fact

text: Roethlisberger and Dickson, Management and the Worker (Harvard University Press, 1939), reported that female assembly workers at the Hawthorne Works showed productivity gains that appeared tied to being observed rather than to specific lighting or break manipulations.
label: reference

text: Workers whose behaviour is being observed as part of a study may increase their productivity simply because they know they are being watched, regardless of the specific conditions being tested.
label: fact

text: Frederick Herzberg, 'One More Time: How Do You Motivate Employees?', Harvard Business Review 46 (1968) 53-62, distinguished hygiene factors such as pay and supervision from motivators such as achievement and recognition that drive satisfaction.
label: reference

text: In workplaces, factors like pay and working conditions mainly prevent dissatisfaction, while genuine motivation tends to come from achievement, recognition, and meaningful work.
label: fact

text: Hackman and Oldham, 'Motivation through the Design of Work: Test of a Theory', Organizational Behavior and Human Performance 16 (1976) 250-279, proposed that five core job characteristics - skill variety, task identity, task significance, autonomy, and feedback - shape intrinsic motivation.
label: reference

text: Jobs that combine varied skills, a clear whole task, meaningful impact, autonomy, and regular feedback tend to produce higher intrinsic motivation in workers.
label: fact

text: McDaniel, Whetzel, Schmidt, and Maurer, 'The Validity of Employment Interviews: A Comprehensive Review and Meta-Analysis', Journal of Applied Psychology 79 (1994) 599-616, reported that structured interviews predict job performance substantially better than unstructured interviews.
label: reference

text: Structured employment interviews with standardised questions and scoring rubrics predict later job performance much more accurately than free-form unstructured interviews.
label: fact

text: James S. Coleman, Equality of Educational Opportunity (U.S. Government Printing Office, 1966), concluded from a survey of over 600,000 American students that family background accounted for more variance in student achievement than measurable school resources.
label: reference

text: In large-scale surveys of American schoolchildren, differences in family socioeconomic background account for more of the variation in academic achievement than differences in school resources.
label: fact

text: Christopher Jencks et al., Inequality: A Reassessment of the Effect of Family and Schooling in America (Basic Books, 1972), argued that equalizing school quality would produce only modest reductions in overall income inequality.
label: reference

text: Equalising school resources across neighbourhoods would likely produce only modest reductions in overall adult income inequality because many other factors drive earnings differences.
label: fact

text: Pierre Bourdieu, 'Cultural Reproduction and Social Reproduction' in Knowledge, Education and Cultural Change (ed. Brown, 1973), argued that schools reward a cultural capital unevenly distributed by class, reproducing social hierarchy across generations.
label: reference

text: Schools tend to reward tastes, language, and knowledge that are more common in middle- and upper-class homes, which helps reproduce class advantages across generations.
label: fact

text: Mark Granovetter, 'The Strength of Weak Ties', American Journal of Sociology 78 (1973) 1360-1380, reported that professional and technical workers in the Boston area who found new jobs typically did so through acquaintances rather than through close friends.
label: reference

text: People looking for jobs more often find useful leads through weak social ties such as acquaintances than through their closest friends, because weak ties connect to different information networks.
label: fact

text: Mark Granovetter, 'Economic Action and Social Structure: The Problem of Embeddedness', American Journal of Sociology 91 (1985) 481-510, argued that economic transactions are persistently embedded in ongoing networks of interpersonal relations rather than occurring among atomized actors.
label: reference

text: Economic exchanges are consistently shaped by the ongoing personal relationships and social networks in which the parties are embedded, not by isolated self-interested calculation alone.
label: fact

text: Brian Uzzi, 'Social Structure and Competition in Interfirm Networks: The Paradox of Embeddedness', Administrative Science Quarterly 42 (1997) 35-67, showed that New York garment firms that relied on a mix of arm's-length and embedded ties outperformed those using only one type of tie.
label: reference

text: Firms tend to perform best when their supply relationships combine close, trust-based ties with a broader set of more transactional relationships rather than relying on only one mode.
label: fact

text: Robert Putnam, Making Democracy Work: Civic Traditions in Modern Italy (Princeton University Press, 1993), found that regions with denser horizontal civic associations had more effective regional governments than regions with sparser civic life.
label: reference

text: Regions with stronger traditions of voluntary civic participation tend to have more effective and responsive local government than regions with weaker associational life.
label: fact

text: Robert Putnam, Bowling Alone: The Collapse and Revival of American Community (Simon and Schuster, 2000), documented long-run declines in membership in civic, religious, and voluntary associations across the United States during the second half of the twentieth century.
label: reference

text: Participation in American civic, religious, and voluntary associations declined substantially over the second half of the twentieth century.
label: fact

text: William Julius Wilson, The Truly Disadvantaged (University of Chicago Press, 1987), argued that deindustrialization and middle-class outmigration left concentrated urban black neighborhoods with high joblessness and social isolation.
label: reference

text: The collapse of manufacturing employment and the departure of middle-class residents from many American inner-city neighborhoods left behind concentrated poverty and social isolation.
label: fact

text: Massey and Denton, American Apartheid: Segregation and the Making of the Underclass (Harvard University Press, 1993), used census tract data to show that black Americans faced unusually high and persistent levels of residential segregation compared with other groups.
label: reference

text: Black Americans have faced unusually high and persistent levels of residential segregation in U.S. metropolitan areas compared with other racial and ethnic groups.
label: fact

text: Chetty, Hendren, Kline, and Saez, 'Where is the Land of Opportunity? The Geography of Intergenerational Mobility in the United States', Quarterly Journal of Economics 129 (2014) 1553-1623, used tax records for 40 million children and their parents to document large regional differences in upward mobility.
label: reference

text: Upward economic mobility varies dramatically across U.S. regions, with some metropolitan areas offering much better chances for children from low-income families to reach higher income brackets than others.
label: fact

text: Samuel Preston, 'The Changing Relation between Mortality and Level of Economic Development', Population Studies 29 (1975) 231-248, showed that life expectancy at a given income level rose substantially during the twentieth century, implying that factors beyond income drove mortality decline.
label: reference

text: Life expectancy rose at every level of income over the twentieth century, indicating that much of the long-run decline in mortality was driven by factors beyond rising income.
label: fact

text: Frank Notestein, 'Population: The Long View' in Food for the World (ed. Schultz, 1945), articulated the demographic transition theory in which mortality declines precede fertility declines during modernization.
label: reference

text: During modernization, societies typically experience a fall in death rates before birth rates drop, producing a period of rapid population growth followed by stabilisation at lower vital rates.
label: fact

text: Sampson, Raudenbush, and Earls, 'Neighborhoods and Violent Crime: A Multilevel Study of Collective Efficacy', Science 277 (1997) 918-924, found that neighborhood collective efficacy predicted lower rates of violence in Chicago even after controlling for concentrated disadvantage.
label: reference

text: Neighborhoods where residents trust one another and are willing to intervene for the common good tend to have lower rates of violent crime, even after accounting for poverty and other disadvantage.
label: fact

text: Cohen and Felson, 'Social Change and Crime Rate Trends: A Routine Activity Approach', American Sociological Review 44 (1979) 588-608, argued that predatory crime requires the convergence in time and space of a motivated offender, a suitable target, and the absence of capable guardians.
label: reference

text: Predatory crime tends to occur when a motivated offender, an attractive target, and a lack of effective guardians come together in the same time and place.
label: fact

text: Wilson and Kelling, 'Broken Windows: The Police and Neighborhood Safety', The Atlantic (March 1982), argued that visible signs of disorder such as broken windows and graffiti signal that no one is in charge and encourage more serious crime.
label: reference

text: Visible signs of neighborhood disorder such as broken windows, graffiti, and litter can signal a lack of social control and encourage additional and more serious criminal behaviour.
label: fact

text: Gottfredson and Hirschi, A General Theory of Crime (Stanford University Press, 1990), proposed that low self-control, formed in childhood and stable across the life course, is the primary individual-level predictor of criminal behaviour.
label: reference

text: Individual differences in self-control established in childhood are one of the strongest and most stable individual-level predictors of later involvement in crime.
label: fact

text: Verba, Schlozman, and Brady, Voice and Equality: Civic Voluntarism in American Politics (Harvard University Press, 1995), showed that political participation in the United States is strongly stratified by socioeconomic resources, civic skills, and recruitment.
label: reference

text: Political participation in the United States is strongly tilted toward citizens with higher income, education, and civic skills, and those who are more often recruited into political activity.
label: fact

text: Philip Converse, 'The Nature of Belief Systems in Mass Publics' in Ideology and Discontent (ed. Apter, 1964), argued that most ordinary citizens have weakly structured and unstable political belief systems compared with political elites.
label: reference

text: Most ordinary citizens hold political opinions that are far less internally consistent and stable over time than the opinions held by political elites and activists.
label: fact

text: Stanley Milgram, 'The Small-World Problem', Psychology Today 1 (1967) 61-67, reported that chains of acquaintances connecting randomly chosen Americans to a distant target person typically contained only about five or six intermediaries.
label: reference

text: Chains of acquaintances connecting two random people in a large population often involve only a handful of intermediaries, a pattern popularly summarised as six degrees of separation.
label: fact

text: Watts and Strogatz, 'Collective Dynamics of Small-World Networks', Nature 393 (1998) 440-442, showed that adding a small number of long-range shortcuts to a regular lattice sharply reduces the average path length while preserving high clustering.
label: reference

text: Many real social and biological networks combine high local clustering with short average path lengths, a pattern that can emerge when a mostly regular network contains a few long-range connections.
label: fact

text: Christakis and Fowler, 'The Spread of Obesity in a Large Social Network over 32 Years', New England Journal of Medicine 357 (2007) 370-379, used Framingham Heart Study data to report that a person's chance of becoming obese rose when a close social contact became obese.
label: reference

text: A person's likelihood of becoming obese tends to rise when people in their close social network also become obese, suggesting that health behaviours spread through social ties.
label: fact

text: Robin Dunbar, 'Neocortex Size as a Constraint on Group Size in Primates', Journal of Human Evolution 22 (1992) 469-493, proposed on the basis of primate neocortex ratios that humans can maintain stable personal relationships with only about 150 other individuals.
label: reference

text: Humans can typically sustain stable meaningful personal relationships with only about 150 other people, a ceiling that appears linked to the size of our social brain.
label: fact

text: Ranehill et al., 'Assessing the Robustness of Power Posing: No Effect on Hormones and Risk Tolerance in a Large Sample of Men and Women', Psychological Science 26 (2015) 653-656, failed to replicate the hormonal and risk-tolerance effects of expansive postures originally reported by Carney, Cuddy, and Yap.
label: reference

text: Large replication attempts have failed to reproduce earlier claims that briefly holding expansive body postures meaningfully changes hormone levels or risk-taking behaviour.
label: fact

text: Hagger et al., 'A Multilab Preregistered Replication of the Ego-Depletion Effect', Perspectives on Psychological Science 11 (2016) 546-573, coordinated 23 laboratories and found essentially no evidence for the classic ego-depletion effect on subsequent self-control tasks.
label: reference

text: A large coordinated replication project found little evidence that briefly exerting self-control measurably degrades performance on a subsequent self-control task, challenging earlier ego-depletion findings.
label: fact

text: Switched from Next.js App Router to Astro for the marketing site after hydration costs pushed Largest Contentful Paint past 3.4 seconds on mid-tier Android devices.
label: decision

text: Marketing pages ship as static Astro 4 islands with React islands hydrated only for the quote calculator and the search dialog, sharing a single shadcn/ui theme token bundle.
label: architecture

text: Migrated the admin dashboard from Create React App to Vite 5 after webpack cold starts crossed 70 seconds on the design team's MacBook Airs.
label: decision

text: The admin dashboard builds with Vite 5 using SWC for transforms, esbuild for prebundling, and a vendor manualChunks split that keeps the recharts bundle outside the first-load JS.
label: architecture

text: Moved product detail pages from on-demand SSR to Incremental Static Regeneration with a 60-second revalidate after origin CPU pegged during price update storms.
label: decision

text: Product pages render via Next.js ISR with revalidate=60, on-demand revalidation triggered by a Kafka consumer on pricing events, and a stale-while-revalidate CDN policy in front.
label: architecture

text: Chose full SSG over SSR for the developer documentation portal because the content is Git-sourced MDX and there is no per-user state to render.
label: decision

text: Docs are pre-rendered by Astro at build time from MDX sources in the monorepo, deployed as immutable static files to Cloudflare Pages with a search index generated at build.
label: architecture

text: Replaced Redux Toolkit with Zustand in the trading console after boilerplate for every new slice slowed feature delivery and discouraged typed selectors.
label: decision

text: Trading console state is split into five Zustand stores (orders, portfolio, market data, UI, session) each with its own persist middleware and immer middleware for nested updates.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Jotai over a tree of React Contexts for the form-heavy onboarding flow after nested providers forced full-tree rerenders on every keystroke.
label: decision

text: Onboarding form state lives in Jotai atoms, grouped by step, with atomFamily used for per-field validation and a selectAtom derived atom feeding the progress indicator.
label: architecture

text: Switched from SWR to TanStack Query v5 because the app needed mutation lifecycle hooks and query invalidation graphs that SWR could not express declaratively.
label: decision

text: Server state is managed by TanStack Query v5 with a global QueryClient configured for 30s stale time, exponential retry backoff, and an Axios wrapper that normalizes error shapes.
label: architecture

text: Moved the darkraise-ui package from React Router v6 to TanStack Router to get end-to-end typed routes and file-based route generation.
label: decision

text: The UI uses TanStack Router with file-based route generation, each route exposing loader, search params schema, and error boundary colocated, and a root route owning the auth guard.
label: architecture

text: Dropped hash-based routing on the embedded analytics widget after customers complained deep links broke when pasted into Slack unfurls.
label: decision

text: The embedded widget uses the History API with a configurable basename so host apps can mount it under /analytics while retaining shareable deep links with standard URLs.
label: architecture

text: Replaced MUI v5 with shadcn/ui after designers could not override the deeply nested Emotion styles without escape-hatch sx props everywhere.
label: decision

text: The component system is a copy-in shadcn/ui library on top of Radix primitives, styled with Tailwind and CVA variants, published internally as @darkraise/ui with tree-shakable exports.
label: architecture

text: Chose Mantine v7 over Chakra v2 for the internal tools after needing polished data grid, date range picker, and rich text editor primitives out of the box.
label: decision

text: Internal tools use Mantine v7 with the Mantine DataTable, Mantine Dates, and Tiptap integration, themed by a single createTheme call driven from a design-token JSON file.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Style Dictionary for design tokens after hex values drifted between Figma, iOS, and the web app and caused three brand-inconsistency bug reports in a month.
label: decision

text: Design tokens are authored in a single tokens.json, transformed by Style Dictionary into CSS variables, Tailwind theme extensions, Swift enums, and Kotlin objects consumed across platforms.
label: architecture

text: Moved the marketing codebase from Sass modules to Tailwind v3 after dead-style audits showed 38% of shipped CSS was unused on mobile.
label: decision

text: Styling uses Tailwind v3 with a design-token preset, tailwind-merge for class reconciliation, and PurgeCSS running against MDX and TSX sources for a final 18 KB CSS bundle.
label: architecture

text: Switched from styled-components to vanilla-extract because runtime CSS-in-JS added 40 ms to hydration on the checkout route.
label: decision

text: Styles compile at build time via vanilla-extract with static theme contracts, generating atomic CSS through Sprinkles and ship zero runtime JS for styling in the checkout bundle.
label: architecture

text: Replaced Formik with react-hook-form in the signup funnel after re-render storms on large field arrays caused dropped keystrokes on low-end Chromebooks.
label: decision

text: Signup forms use react-hook-form with uncontrolled inputs, Zod resolvers for validation, and a FormProvider at each step so field-array rows rerender in isolation.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Zod schemas shared across client and server after duplicate yup and Joi validators drifted and rejected valid submissions on the edge.
label: decision

text: Form schemas are defined once in a shared @darkraise/schemas package using Zod, consumed by react-hook-form resolvers on the client and by Fastify route validation on the server.
label: architecture

text: Replaced localStorage JWT storage with httpOnly SameSite=Strict cookies after a dependency with a postinstall script exfiltrated tokens in a preview build.
label: decision

text: The SPA authenticates against a same-origin /auth proxy that sets httpOnly Secure SameSite=Strict session cookies, with CSRF tokens issued per form and verified by the API gateway.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Auth.js (NextAuth v5) over a hand-rolled OIDC client because refresh-token rotation and multi-provider linking kept regressing under test.
label: decision

text: Authentication in the Next.js app is managed by Auth.js v5 with the Prisma adapter, Keycloak and GitHub providers, and middleware gating every /app route on a valid session cookie.
label: architecture

text: Switched the legacy webpack 5 pipeline to Rspack after production builds consistently exceeded the nine-minute CI budget on large branches.
label: decision

text: The build pipeline runs Rspack 1.0 with the webpack-compatible config, SWC loaders, persistent filesystem cache on the CI runner, and a module-federation remote for the plugin surface.
label: architecture

text: Chose Rollup over Vite library mode for the published UI package because we needed multi-format output plus bundled .d.ts files with precise export maps.
label: decision

text: The @darkraise/ui package is built by Rollup 4 emitting ESM and CJS bundles, dts-rollup-generated type bundles, and a package.json with fine-grained exports per component entry.
label: architecture

text: Replaced Jest with Vitest after ESM-only dependencies broke the transform pipeline and ts-jest startup took 11 seconds on a two-test file.
label: decision

text: Unit tests run under Vitest 1.6 in happy-dom mode, parallelized with eight workers, sharing the Vite dev config so module resolution matches the production bundle exactly.
label: architecture

text: Migrated E2E tests from Cypress to Playwright after flake on cross-origin iframes and a missing multi-tab model made auth-flow tests unreliable.
label: decision

text: E2E suites run in Playwright with three projects (chromium, firefox, webkit), sharded across four CI runners, using a storageState fixture to skip login for non-auth scenarios.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Chromatic for visual regression after three UI bugs shipped to production that a diff would have caught before review.
label: decision

text: Storybook 8 stories are published to Chromatic on every PR, with baseline snapshots keyed on the main branch, TurboSnap enabled to skip unchanged components, and a required GitHub check.
label: architecture

text: Chose Playwright's toHaveScreenshot over a SaaS visual tool because we already ran Playwright in CI and did not want another vendor managing screenshot baselines.
label: decision

text: Visual regression runs as a dedicated Playwright project with deterministic fonts, masked timestamps, and PNG baselines stored in Git LFS under tests/visual/__screenshots__.
label: architecture

text: Adopted axe-core in CI after a customer audit flagged 14 WCAG 2.2 AA violations that had slipped through manual review for a year.
label: decision

text: Accessibility checks run as a Playwright project invoking axe-core on every key page, failing CI on serious or critical impact rules and producing a HTML report published as a job artifact.
label: architecture

text: Chose the Storybook addon-a11y to shift accessibility left after most issues originated at the component level rather than the page composition.
label: decision

text: Every Storybook story runs the addon-a11y checks in the Storybook test-runner under axe, with a shared axe config that disables color-contrast on tokens-sourced swatches.
label: architecture

text: Switched from i18next to FormatJS after translators complained about missing ICU plural and select support on the billing invoices page.
label: decision

text: Localization uses FormatJS with ICU MessageFormat strings, messages extracted to JSON by formatjs extract, and language bundles loaded on demand with dynamic import() per locale.
label: architecture

text: Moved locale resolution from the client to the edge after users hitting the German site briefly saw English content while the bundle loaded.
label: decision

text: Locale is detected at a Cloudflare Worker by Accept-Language and a user cookie, injected into the HTML as a __LOCALE__ global, and consumed by React Intl providers during SSR hydration.
label: architecture

text: Adopted LaunchDarkly over env-variable gates after the pricing experiment needed percentage rollouts and per-account targeting within a single deploy.
label: decision

text: The SPA bootstraps LaunchDarkly on mount with user identity keyed on account_id, streams flag updates via SSE, and wraps gated UI in a FeatureFlag component that short-circuits render.
label: architecture

text: Chose OpenFeature with flagd for internal tool flags because data residency rules blocked sending user identifiers to a SaaS flag provider.
label: decision

text: Internal web apps evaluate flags through the OpenFeature React SDK against a flagd sidecar at localhost:8013, with rule definitions synced from a Git repository and reloaded on change.
label: architecture

text: Replaced Google Analytics 4 with self-hosted PostHog after EU privacy review required first-party telemetry and session replay without third-party cookies.
label: decision

text: Client analytics call a self-hosted PostHog instance via a reverse-proxied /ingest path, with autocapture enabled, session replay sampled at 10%, and identify fired after login.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Segment with server-side destinations after ad blockers dropped about 22% of client-side events on the marketing funnel.
label: decision

text: Events are sent client-side to a same-origin /collect edge endpoint that forwards to Segment server-side, which fans out to Mixpanel, Braze, and a BigQuery destination.
label: architecture

text: Adopted nested React Error Boundaries tied to Sentry after a single uncaught render error in the sidebar blanked the entire dashboard for five minutes.
label: decision

text: The app wraps each top-level route and each async island in an ErrorBoundary that reports to Sentry with a scoped tag and renders a localized fallback UI with a retry button.
label: architecture

text: Enabled Sentry Session Replay on error-only sampling after support could not reproduce intermittent drag-and-drop bugs reported by enterprise users.
label: decision

text: The SPA configures Sentry browser SDK with replaysSessionSampleRate=0 and replaysOnErrorSampleRate=1, masking all text inputs and blocking screenshots on the compliance-flagged routes.
label: architecture

text: Adopted React 19 streaming SSR with Suspense boundaries after the product page's server render blocked on a slow reviews call, delaying Time To First Byte by 900 ms.
label: decision

text: Product pages stream through React 19 renderToPipeableStream with Suspense boundaries around reviews, recommendations, and inventory, each resolved independently from the backing service.
label: architecture

text: Chose route-level lazy() boundaries over component-level after bundle analysis showed admin-only views were loaded for every signed-in customer.
label: decision

text: Every TanStack Router route component is imported via lazy() with a shared Suspense boundary showing a skeleton, and router-level preload runs on link hover for primary navigation.
label: architecture

text: Moved the dashboard from REST to GraphQL with a single endpoint because the widgets page made 14 sequential calls that could not be parallelized cleanly.
label: decision

text: The dashboard queries a federated GraphQL gateway through urql with Graphcache, persisted operation IDs, and a single websocket subscription channel for live widget updates.
label: architecture

text: Chose tRPC over a hand-written REST client for the internal admin app because the teams own both ends of the wire in the same TypeScript monorepo.
label: decision

text: The admin app calls a tRPC v11 router over HTTP batch links, types shared from the backend package, and uses superjson transformers so Date and Decimal values round-trip unchanged.
label: architecture

text: Adopted React Server Components in the Next.js app for the reporting surface after client-only data fetching left large hydration payloads on routes nobody interacted with.
label: decision

text: Reporting pages render as Server Components that fetch from Postgres directly through a server-only data layer, with Client Components pushed to leaves like filters and chart legends.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Workbox-generated service workers after field technicians in low-connectivity warehouses lost form progress when the Wi-Fi dropped mid-shift.
label: decision

text: The field-ops PWA uses a Workbox service worker with a StaleWhileRevalidate strategy for APIs, a CacheFirst strategy for shell assets, and a background sync queue for pending form POSTs.
label: architecture

text: Chose IndexedDB via Dexie over localStorage for the draft editor because quotas and write latency on localStorage broke autosave for documents over 1 MB.
label: decision

text: Drafts are persisted to IndexedDB through Dexie 4 with a versioned schema, an autosave hook debounced at 400 ms, and a background reconciliation worker that diffs local drafts against the server.
label: architecture

text: Picked Nx for the frontend monorepo over Turborepo because the team needed generators, module-boundary lint rules, and a dependency graph visualizer on day one.
label: decision

text: The frontend monorepo is organized with Nx 19, enforcing tag-based import boundaries between feature, ui, and data-access libs, with Nx Cloud remote cache shared across developers and CI.
label: architecture

text: Replaced a 240 KB icon font with tree-shakable SVG React components via SVGR after the font blocked First Contentful Paint on slow 3G.
label: decision

text: Icons are authored as SVG files, compiled by SVGR into typed React components with aria-hidden defaults, and imported per-icon so only referenced glyphs land in the route bundle.
label: architecture

text: Chose visx over Recharts for the finance dashboard because dense time-series plots needed bespoke axes and Canvas fallback for 40k-point series.
label: decision

text: Finance charts are composed from visx primitives on top of a shared scale provider, SVG for <5k points and a Canvas renderer above that threshold, with a d3-time axis shared between both paths.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Framer Motion over CSS keyframes for route transitions after designers needed shared-layout animations between the list and detail views.
label: decision

text: Route transitions use Framer Motion's layout animations, with a LayoutGroup at the router outlet and AnimatePresence wrapping the route tree so exit animations run before unmount.
label: architecture

text: Replaced react-dnd with dnd-kit on the kanban board after keyboard-only users could not reorder cards and the HTML5 backend dropped on touch devices.
label: decision

text: The kanban board uses dnd-kit with the sortable preset, keyboard and pointer sensors configured, a DragOverlay rendered outside the scrollable column, and accessible announcements on drop.
label: architecture

text: Switched from react-window to TanStack Virtual on the audit log page because variable row heights and a sticky group header caused visible jumps on scroll.
label: decision

text: The audit log uses TanStack Virtual's useVirtualizer with dynamic row measurement, overscan of 8, and a sticky group header rendered outside the virtualized range to avoid measurement drift.
label: architecture

text: Turned on TypeScript strict mode across the SPA after three production incidents traced back to undefined prop access that PropTypes warnings did not catch in production builds.
label: decision

text: The SPA compiles with tsconfig strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes, and verbatimModuleSyntax, with a project-references graph splitting app, ui, and data-access layers.
label: architecture

text: Switched from npm to pnpm for the frontend workspace after node_modules size on a fresh clone exceeded 2.1 GB and installs took over four minutes.
label: decision

text: The workspace uses pnpm 9 with a content-addressable store, a locked packageManager field in root package.json, and a .npmrc enforcing public-hoist-pattern=[] to catch phantom deps.
label: architecture

text: Adopted ESLint flat config with typescript-eslint v8 after the legacy .eslintrc chain across packages drifted and produced inconsistent rules per workspace.
label: decision

text: Linting runs from a single eslint.config.mjs at the monorepo root with scoped overrides per package, typescript-eslint v8 type-aware rules, and a Prettier disabled-rules block to avoid conflicts.
label: architecture

text: Switched the SFT pipeline from DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 to PyTorch FSDP after memory fragmentation killed the last two 70B runs past step 4000.
label: decision

text: SFT jobs run on 8xH100 nodes with PyTorch FSDP full-shard strategy, bf16 mixed precision, gradient checkpointing on every other transformer block, and Weights & Biases for metric streaming.
label: architecture

text: Adopted 4-way tensor parallelism on top of data parallel after single-GPU activation memory for the 34B model spilled into host RAM and wrecked throughput.
label: decision

text: The 34B pretraining topology uses TP=4 within each 8-GPU node and DP=16 across nodes, with NCCL over a 400 Gb/s InfiniBand fabric and activation recomputation in every MLP block.
label: architecture

text: Picked Lion over AdamW for the 7B continued-pretrain run after an ablation showed comparable loss at 40% less optimiser state memory.
label: decision

text: Continued-pretraining uses the Lion optimiser at lr=3e-5 with beta1=0.9, beta2=0.99, weight_decay=0.1, and a distributed ShardedOptimizer wrapper checkpointed every 1000 steps.
label: architecture

text: Moved the pretraining corpus from Hugging Face streaming to WebDataset shards on S3 after DataLoader stalls throttled effective throughput below 45% MFU.
label: decision

text: Pretraining data lives as 8 GB WebDataset tar shards on S3, prefetched by a torchdata DataPipe with 16 worker processes per node and a 2 GB on-disk local cache for hot shards.
label: architecture

text: Decided to retrain the SentencePiece tokenizer from scratch on the code-heavy mix after OOV rate on Rust and Solidity files exceeded 11% with the inherited Llama tokenizer.
label: decision

text: The tokenizer is a 64k-vocabulary SentencePiece unigram model trained on 120 GB of deduplicated code and prose, with byte fallback enabled and NFC normalisation applied before encoding.
label: architecture

text: Locked the whole training stack to bf16 after fp16 runs on the reward model diverged twice at step 9000 with loss-scale underflow.
label: decision

text: All forward, backward, and optimiser-update passes run in bf16 on H100 tensor cores, with master weights kept in bf16 and no GradScaler since dynamic loss scaling is disabled.
label: architecture

text: Adopted torch.distributed.checkpoint asynchronous saving after synchronous full-state checkpoints stalled the job for 90 seconds every 2000 steps.
label: decision

text: Checkpoints are written every 2000 steps through torch.distributed.checkpoint in async mode to a dedicated S3 bucket with per-rank sharded tensors and a single metadata file resolved by the coordinator rank.
label: architecture

text: Standardised on EleutherAI lm-evaluation-harness over an in-house eval script after two engineers reported different MMLU numbers on the same checkpoint.
label: decision

text: Offline evals run lm-evaluation-harness v0.4 inside a pinned container on a dedicated 2xA100 box, scoring MMLU, HellaSwag, ARC-Challenge, GSM8K, and TruthfulQA with a fixed seed and loglikelihood requests.
label: architecture

text: Picked Ray Tune with ASHA over a grid search after the twelve-point learning-rate sweep ate three weeks of GPU time for no meaningful gain.
label: decision

text: Hyperparameter search runs Ray Tune 2.10 with the ASHA scheduler over 64 concurrent trials on a dedicated 4-node A100 cluster, reporting into a shared MLflow tracking server.
label: architecture

text: Migrated experiment tracking from local TensorBoard event files to Weights & Biases after cross-run comparisons across branches became impossible to share with reviewers.
label: decision

text: Every training job streams metrics, system stats, and artefact manifests into Weights & Biases under the darkmem-llm project, with per-branch groups and per-run config hashes for deterministic replay.
label: architecture

text: Moved model artefacts from an NFS share to a content-addressed S3 layout after two engineers overwrote each other's checkpoints on the same path.
label: decision

text: Final and intermediate checkpoints live under s3://darkmem-artefacts/ keyed by sha256 of the state_dict manifest, with a sqlite index mapping run_id, step, and git_sha to the corresponding S3 prefix.
label: architecture

text: Chose a Bradley-Terry pairwise reward model over a pointwise scalar regressor after inter-annotator agreement on absolute scores collapsed below 0.4 kappa.
label: decision

text: The reward model is a 7B transformer with a scalar head trained on 180k Bradley-Terry preference pairs, using a margin-ranking loss with beta=0.1 and a 10% chosen/rejected swap regulariser.
label: architecture

text: Swapped the PPO rollout loop for DPO after PPO hyperparameter sensitivity caused three consecutive runs to collapse into repetition within 500 steps.
label: decision

text: The alignment stage is a single-phase DPO run over 120k preference pairs with beta=0.1, reference model frozen in bf16, and a constant lr=5e-7 schedule over 3 epochs.
label: architecture

text: Adopted the TRL SFTTrainer over a hand-rolled Trainer subclass after the packing and response-only loss masking code kept drifting between the chat and code variants.
label: decision

text: SFT runs on TRL 0.9 SFTTrainer with sequence packing enabled at 8192 tokens, DataCollatorForCompletionOnlyLM masking the prompt, and a Hugging Face Accelerate launcher for FSDP configuration.
label: architecture

text: Chose QLoRA with 4-bit NF4 quantisation for the instruction-tune experiments after full fine-tune on the 13B base blew the 80 GB VRAM budget per GPU.
label: decision

text: Instruction tuning uses QLoRA with bitsandbytes NF4 quantisation, LoRA adapters of rank 64 and alpha 16 on all linear layers, paged AdamW 8-bit optimiser, and merged weights exported to safetensors at the end.
label: architecture

text: Set DPO beta to 0.05 for the safety-tuned variant after higher beta values made the model refuse benign prompts at a 9% false-positive rate on the internal eval set.
label: decision

text: The safety DPO run trains the 7B SFT checkpoint for two epochs at beta=0.05 over 60k harmlessness-preference pairs, with ref_model shared across ranks and reported win-rate on a held-out 2k-prompt slice.
label: architecture

text: Adopted a fast slice-eval every 250 steps after full MMLU at checkpoint time meant regressions were only caught after an eight-hour run completed.
label: decision

text: Training launches a sidecar eval worker that every 250 steps runs a 500-example slice covering MMLU-STEM, GSM8K-100, and an internal refusal probe, reporting deltas back into the W&B run as custom charts.
label: architecture

text: Enabled early stopping with patience 5 on eval perplexity after three long runs overfit past step 18k with no validation-loss improvement for 10k steps.
label: decision

text: The SFT trainer uses a patience-5 early-stopping callback on held-out eval loss, checkpointing the best state and aborting the remainder of the schedule when patience is exhausted.
label: architecture

text: Raised gradient accumulation from 4 to 16 after reducing micro-batch size to fit the 70B model, targeting a constant global batch size of 1024 sequences.
label: decision

text: The 70B SFT run uses a per-device micro batch of 1, gradient accumulation of 16, and 64-way data parallelism for a fixed global batch of 1024 sequences, with all-reduce fused into the backward pass.
label: architecture

text: Switched from linear decay to a cosine schedule with a 2% warmup after the earlier run's loss curve showed a sharp plateau at the 40% mark of training.
label: decision

text: The learning-rate schedule is a single cosine decay from lr=2e-5 to 2e-6 over 30k steps with a 600-step linear warmup, implemented via transformers.get_cosine_schedule_with_warmup.
label: architecture

text: Added a MinHashLSH near-dedup pass over the raw web crawl after a memorisation probe showed 2.3% of training strings appeared verbatim in held-out eval prompts.
label: decision

text: The pretraining data pipeline runs a Spark MinHashLSH job with 128 permutations and Jaccard threshold 0.8, emitting a deduplicated Parquet dataset keyed by document hash before tokenisation.
label: architecture

text: Switched from full activation recomputation to selective checkpointing on only attention blocks after profiling showed the MLPs were 30% cheaper to rerun.
label: decision

text: Activation checkpointing wraps only the attention submodule in each transformer block via torch.utils.checkpoint, keeping MLP activations resident and reducing step time by 18% on the 34B run.
label: architecture

text: Upgraded to FlashAttention-3 on the H100 fleet after kernel benchmarks showed 1.7x throughput over FA-2 for the 8192-context training workload.
label: decision

text: All attention layers use FlashAttention-3 with FP8 accumulation paths disabled, window_size left at defaults, and a fallback to FA-2 on the older A100 pre-training nodes through a runtime dispatch shim.
label: architecture

text: Adopted a two-phase context-length curriculum after directly training at 32k from step zero wasted 35% of compute on padding within shorter documents.
label: decision

text: Pretraining runs 80% of tokens at 4k context and 20% at 32k with linearly interpolated RoPE theta scaling, using the same tokenised corpus reshuffled into length-bucketed packs per phase.
label: architecture

text: Chose YaRN over linear RoPE scaling for the long-context extension after linear scaling degraded needle-in-a-haystack recall below 60% past 16k tokens.
label: decision

text: The 32k-context variant applies YaRN scaling with alpha=1, beta=32, and an attention temperature factor of 0.1, fine-tuned for 4B tokens of long-document data on top of the 4k base checkpoint.
label: architecture

text: Added response-length normalisation to the reward signal after RLHF-trained outputs drifted to verbose essays that scored higher purely from length bias.
label: decision

text: The RLHF reward pipeline subtracts a log-length penalty (alpha=0.02) from the raw reward-model score and clips the result to [-3, 3] before feeding it into the DPO or PPO loss.
label: architecture

text: Added a 15% self-instruct synthetic mix after ablation showed it lifted GSM8K by 4 points without hurting HumanEval performance.
label: decision

text: The SFT dataset is a 1.2M-example mix of 70% human-written instructions, 15% self-instruct expansions from a Llama-3-70B teacher, and 15% code-specific synthetic reasoning pairs, deduplicated against all eval prompts.
label: architecture

text: Restricted the code pretraining corpus to permissive licenses only after legal review flagged GPL contamination in two downstream customer-facing builds.
label: decision

text: The code pretraining corpus is a 420 GB filtered slice of The Stack v2 limited to MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, and ISC licenses, with file-level license detection via scancode-toolkit and a SHA-256 dedup pass.
label: architecture

text: Pinned the chat template in tokenizer_config.json after downstream serving drifted from the training-time format and caused a 6-point regression on IFEval.
label: decision

text: The released tokenizer ships with a fixed Jinja chat_template rendering <|im_start|>role\ncontent<|im_end|> markers, matching the SFT training wrapper exactly and covered by a unit test on every release.
label: architecture

text: Replaced fixed KL coefficient with an adaptive KL controller after PPO runs either collapsed to degenerate outputs or failed to move off the reference policy.
label: decision

text: The PPO loop uses an adaptive KL controller targeting KL=6 nats per token, updating the coefficient every rollout batch of 512 prompts with a step size of 0.1 and clipped advantage normalisation.
label: architecture

text: Adopted vLLM for PPO rollouts after the HuggingFace generate loop capped rollout throughput at 40 tokens per second per GPU.
label: decision

text: PPO rollouts run through a dedicated vLLM 0.5 server pool of 4xH100 with tensor parallelism 2, serving the current policy via a continuous-batching API that the trainer hits with sampling_params per prompt.
label: architecture

text: Added an AdvBench and JailbreakBench regression on every candidate release after an unrelated SFT change silently regressed refusal rate on harmful requests by 12 points.
label: decision

text: The release pipeline runs a 400-prompt adversarial eval against vLLM-served candidates, reporting attack-success-rate per category into W&B and blocking promotion if the rate exceeds the prior release by more than 1%.
label: architecture

text: Reweighted the domain mix to 45% code, 30% web, 20% books, 5% math after ablation showed the prior 70% web mix plateaued on HumanEval below 40%.
label: decision

text: The pretraining data sampler draws document batches with per-domain Dirichlet weights (code 0.45, web 0.30, books 0.20, math 0.05) re-normalised every 500M tokens and logged as a stacked-area chart in W&B.
label: architecture

text: Switched the launcher from Accelerate to plain torchrun after silent rank-binding mismatches on multi-node jobs caused NCCL timeouts at init.
label: decision

text: Multi-node training is launched by torchrun with rdzv_backend=c10d and a dedicated etcd coordinator, using SLURM srun only to allocate nodes and export NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME for InfiniBand.
label: architecture

text: Added a softmax logit cap of 30 after the pretraining loss spiked to NaN at step 11k when a single head produced logits in the hundreds.
label: decision

text: The model applies a tanh-based soft logit cap of 30 on the final LM-head output, following the Gemma 2 recipe, implemented as a fused triton kernel to avoid an extra pass over the vocabulary tensor.
label: architecture

text: Moved tokenisation out of the DataLoader into an offline Spark job after on-the-fly tokenisation bottlenecked CPU utilisation at 98% and starved the GPUs.
label: decision

text: The pretraining corpus is pre-tokenised by a Spark job into 4k-token packed sequences stored as int32 Arrow files on S3, read at training time with a zero-copy memory-mapped loader and no per-batch tokenisation.
label: architecture

text: Mandated full deterministic seeding (torch, numpy, python random, cuDNN, NCCL) after two nominally identical runs diverged in eval loss by 0.02 nats.
label: decision

text: Every training job seeds torch, numpy, random, and os.environ['PYTHONHASHSEED'] from a single run_id, sets torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True), and pins cuDNN benchmark off and NCCL_ALGO to Ring.
label: architecture

text: Built a step-granular resume mechanism after a node preemption at step 24k forced the entire run to restart from the last epoch boundary.
label: decision

text: Resume logic reads the latest torch.distributed.checkpoint shard plus a separate dataloader-state file recording (epoch, shard_id, sample_offset, rng_state) so training resumes within one step of the preemption point.
label: architecture

text: Lowered the global-norm gradient clip from 1.0 to 0.5 after instability spikes on the 70B run correlated with isolated grad-norm excursions above 3.0.
label: decision

text: Gradient clipping is applied globally at max_norm=0.5 on the all-reduced gradients under FSDP, with the pre- and post-clip norms logged every step for anomaly detection.
label: architecture

text: Adopted depth-scaled residual initialisation after the 40-layer model diverged within 200 steps using standard transformers init.
label: decision

text: Residual projection weights are initialised with std = 0.02 / sqrt(2 * n_layers) following the GPT-NeoX recipe, while all other linear layers use torch default Xavier-uniform init.
label: architecture

text: Chose 8-way expert parallelism for the 8x22B MoE run after all-to-all bandwidth profiling showed EP=8 kept comms under 15% of step time.
label: decision

text: The MoE stage runs 8-way expert parallelism with 4-way tensor parallelism and 4-way data parallelism on a 128xH100 cluster, using Megablocks grouped-GEMM kernels and a capacity factor of 1.25.
label: architecture

text: Added a 0.01 coefficient load-balancing loss after two experts in the MoE collapsed to near-zero utilisation within the first 3k steps.
label: decision

text: The MoE router applies a Switch Transformer style auxiliary loss with coefficient 0.01 plus a z-loss of 1e-3 on router logits, with per-expert token-usage histograms exported every 500 steps.
label: architecture

text: Froze lm-evaluation-harness to commit d1abf5a after a point release silently changed MMLU prompt formatting and invalidated two months of comparison runs.
label: decision

text: Evaluation runs always execute inside a pinned Docker image containing lm-evaluation-harness commit d1abf5a, transformers 4.41, torch 2.3, and a hash-verified tokenizer_config bundle per candidate model.
label: architecture

text: Enabled torch.compile only on the transformer block after compiling the full forward caused recompilation storms whenever batch shapes changed.
label: decision

text: torch.compile is applied at the TransformerBlock module level with mode=max-autotune-no-cudagraphs and dynamic=False, compiled once per distinct sequence-length bucket with a 16-entry cache.
label: architecture

text: Added a KenLM perplexity filter on raw web data after inspection showed roughly 8% of docs were auto-generated SEO spam with degenerate n-gram stats.
label: decision

text: The data pipeline runs a KenLM 5-gram model trained on Wikipedia over every candidate document, dropping the top and bottom 1% by log-perplexity and logging the filtered histogram per snapshot.
label: architecture

text: Added a human preference gate (pairwise battles on 200 prompts) before any release after two models with identical benchmark scores had drastically different user feedback.
label: decision

text: Release candidates are evaluated by a pairwise side-by-side UI that shows 200 curated prompts to three in-house raters, with Bradley-Terry aggregation and a required win-rate of 55% over the prior release.
label: architecture

text: Introduced a 5% replay buffer from the original SFT mix during the domain-specific fine-tune after the math-tuned variant regressed 7 points on generic instruction-following.
label: decision

text: Domain fine-tuning draws each batch as 95% domain data and 5% uniformly sampled general-SFT examples from a pre-built replay shard, with the replay fraction tracked in W&B per step.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Best-Fit-Decreasing sequence packing after random packing left 14% of every 8k-token pack as pad tokens on the SFT dataset.
label: decision

text: SFT training packs multiple conversations into each 8192-token sequence using a Best-Fit-Decreasing packer with EOS boundary tokens and an attention mask that isolates conversations within the same pack.
label: architecture

text: Ran a Constitutional AI revision pass after the first safety DPO produced overly terse refusals that users flagged as unhelpful.
label: decision

text: The safety stack appends a Constitutional AI revision phase: 40k prompts are generated from the SFT model, revised by a critic-model loop against a 23-rule constitution, and the (original, revised) pairs feed a second DPO at beta=0.1.
label: architecture

text: Established a shadow-eval policy requiring every data or hyperparameter change to ship alongside a 7B ablation run after a quiet mix change cost two weeks of 70B compute.
label: decision

text: Every non-trivial training PR triggers a shadow 7B run on a dedicated 8xA100 pool for 5B tokens, with automated eval deltas on MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval, and IFEval posted as a comment on the PR before approval.
label: architecture

text: Switched the mobile client from REST to gRPC-Web after the battery cost of JSON-over-HTTPS caught up with us during the week-long field trial in Jakarta.
label: decision

text: Mobile clients call a gRPC-Web endpoint at /svc with protobuf schemas versioned under the v2/ package and backed by Envoy translating to internal gRPC on port 9000.
label: architecture

text: Chose Apollo Federation v2 over a BFF layer because three product teams kept redefining the same User type in slightly incompatible shapes.
label: decision

text: The public GraphQL API is served by an Apollo Router 1.50 gateway composing four subgraphs (users, catalog, billing, orders) published to Apollo Studio with schema checks on every PR.
label: architecture

text: Adopted URL-path versioning (/v1, /v2) over header-based versioning after support tickets kept tracing back to customers who forgot the Accept-Version header.
label: decision

text: The public HTTP API mounts versions at /v1 and /v2 path prefixes with FastAPI sub-applications, and an Nginx rule rewrites bare paths to /v1 for legacy clients.
label: architecture

text: Switched list endpoints from offset+limit to opaque cursor pagination after a customer's 400k-row export consistently timed out past page 800.
label: decision

text: List endpoints return a base64-encoded cursor that packs (last_id, last_sort_key, tenant_id) and the server decodes it into a keyset query with LIMIT 200 plus a next_cursor field.
label: architecture

text: Standardized on RFC 7807 application/problem+json error bodies over the in-house {code,msg} shape after the SDK team could not generate typed error classes reliably.
label: decision

text: All public endpoints return errors as application/problem+json documents with type, title, status, detail, instance, and a vendor-prefixed errors[] array generated from a shared Pydantic model.
label: architecture

text: Adopted OAuth2 client_credentials with JWT assertions over long-lived API keys after a leaked key in a public GitHub repo took 48 hours to rotate across every partner.
label: decision

text: Partner integrations authenticate via OAuth2 client_credentials flow backed by a Keycloak realm issuing 10-minute access tokens scoped by audience and signed with per-partner RS256 key pairs.
label: architecture

text: Chose a Redis-backed token-bucket rate limiter over fixed-window counters after bursty webhook retries kept tripping the 429 threshold for well-behaved clients.
label: decision

text: Rate limiting runs as an Envoy filter that calls a Redis Lua script implementing token-bucket with per-route capacity and refill rate, keyed by (tenant_id, api_key_hash).
label: architecture

text: Moved webhook delivery from inline HTTP calls to a durable outbox plus Svix after a midnight DB failover silently dropped an hour of customer.created notifications.
label: decision

text: Webhooks are delivered by Svix reading a Postgres outbox table through CDC, with per-endpoint exponential backoff up to 72 hours, HMAC signatures, and a replay UI for ops.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Stripe-style Idempotency-Key headers on payment and provisioning endpoints after a double-submitted form charged two customers twice on retry.
label: decision

text: Mutating endpoints require an Idempotency-Key header whose value is stored with the response body and status in a Redis cache for 24 hours, keyed by (api_key, path, key).
label: architecture

text: Chose Confluent Schema Registry with Protobuf over embedding schemas in each message after a consumer team shipped a producer that broke two downstream services at once.
label: decision

text: All Kafka topics carry Protobuf-encoded messages whose schema id is fetched from a Confluent Schema Registry cluster with FULL_TRANSITIVE compatibility and subject naming of <topic>-value.
label: architecture

text: Switched to an OpenAPI-first workflow where the spec is the source of truth after hand-written docs diverged from the server behavior on three consecutive releases.
label: decision

text: The public API is defined in a single openapi.yaml stored in a shared repo, with FastAPI routes generated by datamodel-code-generator and client SDKs by openapi-generator on every merge.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Speakeasy for typed SDK generation over hand-written clients because customer-reported bugs in the Python and Go SDKs kept diverging from each other.
label: decision

text: SDKs for Python, TypeScript, Go, and Java are generated from the OpenAPI spec by Speakeasy on every release tag, published to language registries and versioned in lockstep with the server.
label: architecture

text: Picked Stoplight Spectral for API linting in CI over ad-hoc reviewers after inconsistent error shapes and missing examples slipped through three pull requests in a week.
label: decision

text: CI runs Spectral against openapi.yaml using the company rule set (required examples, consistent error schemas, snake_case fields) and blocks merges on any error-level finding.
label: architecture

text: Adopted a strict additive-only evolution policy for v1 after renaming a field in a bugfix release broke a partner integration and triggered a contract penalty.
label: decision

text: A custom openapi-diff CI check flags any removed field, renamed field, narrowed type, or new required parameter on v1 routes and routes breaking changes to a v2 spec file instead.
label: architecture

text: Switched the high-frequency trading sync endpoint from JSON to MessagePack after p95 payload serialization cost dominated the 4 ms budget on commodity hardware.
label: decision

text: The /sync endpoint negotiates application/msgpack via Accept headers, serializing order snapshots with msgpack-python using bin_type=True and strict_types=True, falling back to JSON when the header is absent.
label: architecture

text: Chose Server-Sent Events over WebSockets for the LLM token-streaming endpoint because the product only needed one-way server-to-client delivery and wanted trivial HTTP/2 multiplexing.
label: decision

text: The /chat/stream endpoint returns text/event-stream with each event carrying a JSON delta, flushed through a FastAPI StreamingResponse behind an Envoy proxy configured for idle_timeout=0 and per_connection_buffer_limit=2MB.
label: architecture

text: Added a POST /v1/batch endpoint mirroring OpenAI's batch semantics after enterprise customers hit per-minute rate limits running 200k classification jobs one at a time.
label: decision

text: The batch API accepts a JSONL upload referencing other endpoints by path and body, stores the job in S3, and a background worker fans it out across a celery queue with a 24-hour completion SLO and signed result URLs.
label: architecture

text: Adopted an RFC-7240-style async pattern (202 Accepted plus Location header) over blocking requests after long-running exports held HTTP connections for up to 40 minutes and blew out the ALB idle timeout.
label: decision

text: Long-running endpoints return 202 Accepted with a Location header pointing to /jobs/{id}, whose state machine (queued, running, succeeded, failed) is persisted in Postgres and polled by clients every 5 seconds until terminal.
label: architecture

text: Kept long-polling on the legacy Android v4 app after a telemetry pass showed 12% of active users still on devices without reliable WebSocket support behind carrier proxies.
label: decision

text: Legacy clients poll /notifications/long-poll with a 25-second server hold implemented by asyncio.wait_for on a Redis Streams XREAD BLOCK call, returning 204 on timeout so the client reissues.
label: architecture

text: Moved webhook fanout off the request hot path after a spiky partner endpoint held the main thread pool and starved synchronous customer requests.
label: decision

text: Domain events publish to an internal NATS JetStream subject, and a dedicated webhook-dispatcher service consumes per-tenant streams and delivers signed HTTPS callbacks with a 30-attempt retry curve.
label: architecture

text: Adopted consumer-driven contract testing with Pact after three integration regressions shipped because unit tests on each side passed while the wire format quietly diverged.
label: decision

text: Consumer teams publish Pact contracts to a Pact Broker on each build, and provider CI runs pact-verifier against the broker's latest tagged contracts before allowing a merge to main.
label: architecture

text: Chose Prism as a mock server over Express-based stubs after frontend and backend teams kept drifting apart on the same endpoint between sprints.
label: decision

text: A Prism container runs the openapi.yaml in dynamic mode in the dev docker-compose stack, serving generated examples and validating outgoing requests against the spec before returning 4xx to the client.
label: architecture

text: Adopted Apollo persisted queries over ad-hoc GraphQL documents after a mis-crafted query from the marketing site pulled 40 MB per pageview and tipped the API over.
label: decision

text: Public GraphQL traffic only accepts SHA256 query hashes registered at build time through Apollo's persisted-queries manifest, with the router refusing any non-persisted operations on the production plane.
label: architecture

text: Tightened the CORS policy from Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * to an explicit allowlist after a pentester leveraged a permissive preflight to chain a token-exfiltration attack.
label: decision

text: The API gateway applies CORS per route using a Redis-backed allowlist of customer-registered origins, only echoing the matched origin on Access-Control-Allow-Origin and never allowing credentials with wildcards.
label: architecture

text: Switched file upload endpoints from single POST to tus-protocol resumable uploads after mobile users on flaky 3G reported a 40% failure rate on uploads larger than 20 MB.
label: decision

text: Uploads run through a tusd 2.4 server behind Nginx, storing chunks in S3 via the tusd s3 backend with 5 MiB part sizes and a 7-day unfinished-upload TTL before multipart abort.
label: architecture

text: Moved large file downloads off the application tier and onto S3 presigned URLs after bandwidth costs on egress through the app servers became the single largest line item.
label: decision

text: The /files/{id}/download endpoint returns a 302 redirect to a 15-minute S3 presigned URL with response-content-disposition set per request, bypassing the app tier for the actual transfer.
label: architecture

text: Adopted HMAC-SHA256 request signing with a replay window after a partner's staging URL leaked into a public paste and started receiving forged callbacks.
label: decision

text: Outbound webhooks carry X-Signature (HMAC-SHA256 of timestamp.body using the per-endpoint secret) and X-Timestamp headers, which the receiver verifies within a 5-minute skew window and checks against a Redis nonce cache.
label: architecture

text: Enforced buf breaking and buf lint in CI after a field reuse on a deprecated tag number caused a silent payload corruption on a downstream Go consumer.
label: decision

text: All .proto files live in a central buf module, with buf breaking --against '.git#branch=main' and buf lint run in GitHub Actions on every PR and buf push to a BSR registry on merge.
label: architecture

text: Migrated from self-hosted Kong to AWS API Gateway for the public edge after the ops team could no longer justify 3 am pages for plugin segfaults.
label: decision

text: Public API routes through AWS API Gateway REST APIs with a Lambda authorizer calling the Keycloak introspection endpoint, WAF rules for top-10 OWASP, and a private integration into an NLB fronting the service mesh.
label: architecture

text: Kept internal service-to-service calls on REST plus Protobuf even after adopting GraphQL for the public API because internal consumers have known fields and don't benefit from selection.
label: decision

text: Internal services speak REST over HTTP/2 with Protobuf bodies under application/x-protobuf, generated from shared .proto files, leaving GraphQL strictly on the public edge served by Apollo Router.
label: architecture

text: Adopted AsyncAPI 3.0 as the spec for Kafka and NATS topics after new hires spent their first week manually tracing which service produced which event.
label: decision
